5cb23c2a4d27bc7ab18a9288ea69629c04ff6ff0:
fix(abi): defer delivery until thread-pending signals are handled

Teach sigsuspend and sigtimedwait to observe per-thread pending signals queued by tkill/tgkill. sigtimedwait now consumes signals from the requested set regardless of the caller's blocked mask, matching the usual sigwait pattern.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points after 14 completed static entries in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/before-riscv64-sigtimedwait-thread.log returned thread-sigtimedwait fail r=-1 errno=11 after tkill(gettid, SIGUSR1). After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/after2-riscv64-sigtimedwait-thread.log returned thread-sigtimedwait ok signo=10. Musl libctest guard stayed at the same known timeout point after 14 passing entries in .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/after2-riscv64-musl-libctest.log. Builds: riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 kernel-only passed.

signal: Report blocked pending signals

Linux rt_sigpending reports pending signals that are blocked by the caller's signal mask. Return the blocked pending mask instead of the unblocked deliverable mask so sigpending() can observe blocked signals such as cancellation-related signals.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest stops in pthread_cancel_points in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log after 14 completed entries.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter6-sigpending/before-riscv64-sigpending.log reported sigpending_probe pending_SIGUSR1=0 after blocking and raising SIGUSR1. After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter6-sigpending/after-riscv64-sigpending.log reported pending_SIGUSR1=1.

Build: make check-kernel-build passed for riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernels.

signal: Validate tgkill thread group

Linux tgkill requires the target TID to belong to the supplied thread-group ID. Return ESRCH when the TID exists outside that group instead of queuing the signal anyway.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log after 14 completed entries; pthread cancellation uses targeted thread signals.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter11-shebang/before3-riscv64-tgkill-tgid.log reported tgkill_wrong_tgid_ret=0 for tgkill(getpid()+1234, gettid(), 0). After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter11-shebang/after-riscv64-tgkill-tgid.log reported tgkill_wrong_tgid_ret=-1 and powered off cleanly.

Builds: make ARCH=riscv64 kernel-only, make ARCH=loongarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, and make ARCH=aarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only passed.

signal: match musl signal frame layout

The baseline riscv64 musl libctest log hangs in pthread_cancel_points, where musl inspects uc_mcontext from the SA_SIGINFO signal frame.

A focused RISC-V signal-frame probe showed the saved PC exposed to musl was a kernel-looking 0x800000000009dc38 before this change. After using the musl/Linux 128-byte sigset_t-sized ucontext mask and the RISC-V mcontext PC slot, the same probe reports a normal user PC 0x15ffc with unchanged RA/SP/TP and exits cleanly.

Builds: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64 kernel-only, aarch64 kernel-only.

signal: keep signal masks per thread

Baseline riscv64 musl libcbench timed out in b_pthread_createjoin_serial1 with no timing line. Before focused run reproduced the same after 16 completed subtests. After moving the signal mask out of shared signal_state and onto task_t, the same musl run reached group end and powered off; pthread create/join serial1=1.315269500s, serial2=1.175918300s, create_serial1=1.467482500s. A glibc focused run also progressed from baseline timeout before serial1 timing to serial1=2.165732900s before later timeout. Builds: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64/aarch64 bringup kernel-only.

signal: honor sigtimedwait timeout

Arm a scheduler wake deadline for rt_sigtimedwait with a nonzero timeout and validate tv_nsec so timed waits return instead of blocking indefinitely.

Focused before/after: riscv64 musl pthread_cancel_points changed from a 180s QEMU timeout with no result to the runner's own timeout and shell return. Full musl libctest improved from baseline 15 started/14 passed before QEMU kill to 217 started/188 passed/29 failed with group end. riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernel builds passed.
aa8e051d5f1a9204c4a7de488b46563238827683:
fix(proc): return the thread id from set_tid_address

Linux set_tid_address returns the caller's thread id, not the thread-group id. Return sys_gettid() after recording clear_child_tid so pthread runtimes see the TID they registered.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points after 14 completed entries in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log. Before implementation returned sys_getpid(); after implementation returns sys_gettid().

Focused validation: set_tid_address probe was built under .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter2-pthread-cancel/set_tid_probe, but guest execution was blocked by missing host mkfs.fat during dev-image rebuild; log saved at .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter2-pthread-cancel/before-riscv64-set_tid_address.log. Build validation passed: make ARCH=riscv64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, make ARCH=loongarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, make ARCH=aarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only.

proc: reject setsid from process group leaders

Linux requires setsid to fail with EPERM when the caller is already a process group leader. Add that guard before assigning a new session and process group.

Focused before/after probe: /bin/setsid_probe after setpgid(0,0) changed from setsid=4 errno=0 to setsid=-1 errno=1. Kernel-only builds passed for riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64.

proc: validate clone3 arguments

Reject invalid clone3 argument sizes, Linux-invalid clone flag combinations, mismatched stack pointer/size fields, and bad CLONE_PIDFD user pointers before creating a task.

Focused riscv64 glibc LTP clone302 before: 4 passed / 3 failed / 1 broken, with extra-size, sighand-no-VM, and thread-no-sighand unexpectedly succeeding before the test timed out. After: clone302 reports 12 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Builds passed: riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 kernel-only.

proc: support pidfd signal delivery

Create pidfd anonymous files for clone3(CLONE_PIDFD), implement pidfd_send_signal through the existing signal permission and delivery paths, and preserve queued siginfo payloads when building user signal frames.

Focused riscv64 glibc LTP clone301 before: 4 passed / 2 failed with pidfd_send_signal ENOSYS and missing child signal. After: 7 passed / 0 failed, including SIGUSR1 delivery and si_value 777. Builds passed: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64 kernel-only, aarch64 kernel-only.

sched: reject invalid priority policies

Return EINVAL from sched_get_priority_min/max for unsupported scheduler policies instead of reporting zero priority bounds.

Focused before/after probe: /bin/sprio kept SCHED_OTHER at max=0 min=0 and SCHED_FIFO at max=99 min=1, while invalid policy 999 changed from max=0/min=0 errno=0 to max=-1/min=-1 errno=22. RISC-V focused run powered off cleanly; riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernel-only builds passed.

futex: Preserve waiters on robust owner death

When processing a robust futex on thread exit, clear the dead TID and preserve FUTEX_WAITERS while setting FUTEX_OWNER_DIED. Leaving the dead TID in place and dropping waiters produced a non-Linux owner-death word for pthread robust mutex recovery.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 glibc libcbench in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-glibc-libcbench.log stops during b_pthread_createjoin_serial2. The current tree already completes that focused libcbench run through group end in .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter5-libcbench-thread/before-riscv64-glibc-libcbench.log, so this iteration used a narrower robust-futex probe.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter5-libcbench-thread/before2-riscv64-robust-owner.log reported robust_word=0x40000005 expected=0xc0000000 status=0x0. After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter5-libcbench-thread/after-riscv64-robust-owner.log reported robust_word=0xc0000000 expected=0xc0000000 status=0x0.

Build: make check-kernel-build passed for riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernels.

oom: prefer newest user task on equal score

Under focused riscv64 musl cyclictest stress, forced OOM pressure previously selected pid 2 user, pid 3 mksh, and pid 4 sh before benchmark workers. After changing equal-score victim selection to preserve pid 2 and choose the newest candidate, the same pressure selected hackbench workers pid 406 downward while the harness roots were not selected. dd1b0ce02ed7fb8170f8a84a0a252d6f4c1c47cb:
fix(abi): fix clone tls argument order

Map RISC-V and AArch64 clone syscall arguments as flags, stack, ptid, tls, ctid while keeping the existing LoongArch ctid/tls order.

abi: pass preadv2 flags from sixth arg

Use the sixth syscall argument for preadv2/pwritev2 flags so the offset high word is not mistaken for flags on asm-generic ABIs.

81cb7c7c3cd0e3ba3f154ed1530c4cb4af521b3e:
fix(abi): honor absolute clock_nanosleep deadlines

Implement TIMER_ABSTIME handling for clock_nanosleep so absolute deadlines are converted to the remaining interval instead of treated as relative sleeps.

Focused tests: before riscv64 clock_abs_tmp elapsed_ms=1488; after elapsed_ms=20. riscv64 glibc cyclictest stayed passing in all four phases; after NO_STRESS_P1 C=1000 Max=363us and NO_STRESS_P8 threads reported 222-997 samples, max 2246us.

time: round nanosleep to scheduler tick

Validate nanosleep requests by rejecting tv_nsec >= 1s and round nonzero sub-tick sleeps up to one scheduler tick, matching the POSIX timer conversion used by clock_nanosleep absolute sleeps.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 glibc LTP clock_nanosleep01 passed 3 invalid-argument checks, then timed out in SEND_SIGINT. Focused after direct clock_nanosleep01 reached 5 passed checks, 2 failures, and the same timeout class. Focused musl cyclictest before/after both timed out in NO_STRESS_P1, so no regression was observed there. riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 kernel-only builds passed.

net: Block local sends on full queues

Local socket delivery returned EAGAIN as soon as the peer receive queue filled, even for blocking sockets. Add a separate queue-space waiter and wake it when reads drain queued messages, while preserving O_NONBLOCK and MSG_DONTWAIT behavior.

e8b93be667d07cdddbd946bfc682c4af9490eb56:
fix(abi): defer delivery until thread-pending signals are handled

Teach sigsuspend and sigtimedwait to observe per-thread pending signals queued by tkill/tgkill. sigtimedwait now consumes signals from the requested set regardless of the caller's blocked mask, matching the usual sigwait pattern.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points after 14 completed static entries in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/before-riscv64-sigtimedwait-thread.log returned thread-sigtimedwait fail r=-1 errno=11 after tkill(gettid, SIGUSR1). After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/after2-riscv64-sigtimedwait-thread.log returned thread-sigtimedwait ok signo=10. Musl libctest guard stayed at the same known timeout point after 14 passing entries in .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter4-thread-reap/after2-riscv64-musl-libctest.log. Builds: riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 kernel-only passed.

signal: Report blocked pending signals

Linux rt_sigpending reports pending signals that are blocked by the caller's signal mask. Return the blocked pending mask instead of the unblocked deliverable mask so sigpending() can observe blocked signals such as cancellation-related signals.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest stops in pthread_cancel_points in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log after 14 completed entries.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter6-sigpending/before-riscv64-sigpending.log reported sigpending_probe pending_SIGUSR1=0 after blocking and raising SIGUSR1. After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter6-sigpending/after-riscv64-sigpending.log reported pending_SIGUSR1=1.

Build: make check-kernel-build passed for riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernels.

signal: Validate tgkill thread group

Linux tgkill requires the target TID to belong to the supplied thread-group ID. Return ESRCH when the TID exists outside that group instead of queuing the signal anyway.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log after 14 completed entries; pthread cancellation uses targeted thread signals.

Focused before: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter11-shebang/before3-riscv64-tgkill-tgid.log reported tgkill_wrong_tgid_ret=0 for tgkill(getpid()+1234, gettid(), 0). After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter11-shebang/after-riscv64-tgkill-tgid.log reported tgkill_wrong_tgid_ret=-1 and powered off cleanly.

Builds: make ARCH=riscv64 kernel-only, make ARCH=loongarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, and make ARCH=aarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only passed.

signal: match musl signal frame layout

The baseline riscv64 musl libctest log hangs in pthread_cancel_points, where musl inspects uc_mcontext from the SA_SIGINFO signal frame.

A focused RISC-V signal-frame probe showed the saved PC exposed to musl was a kernel-looking 0x800000000009dc38 before this change. After using the musl/Linux 128-byte sigset_t-sized ucontext mask and the RISC-V mcontext PC slot, the same probe reports a normal user PC 0x15ffc with unchanged RA/SP/TP and exits cleanly.

Builds: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64 kernel-only, aarch64 kernel-only.

signal: keep signal masks per thread

Baseline riscv64 musl libcbench timed out in b_pthread_createjoin_serial1 with no timing line. Before focused run reproduced the same after 16 completed subtests. After moving the signal mask out of shared signal_state and onto task_t, the same musl run reached group end and powered off; pthread create/join serial1=1.315269500s, serial2=1.175918300s, create_serial1=1.467482500s. A glibc focused run also progressed from baseline timeout before serial1 timing to serial1=2.165732900s before later timeout. Builds: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64/aarch64 bringup kernel-only.

signal: honor sigtimedwait timeout

Arm a scheduler wake deadline for rt_sigtimedwait with a nonzero timeout and validate tv_nsec so timed waits return instead of blocking indefinitely.

Focused before/after: riscv64 musl pthread_cancel_points changed from a 180s QEMU timeout with no result to the runner's own timeout and shell return. Full musl libctest improved from baseline 15 started/14 passed before QEMU kill to 217 started/188 passed/29 failed with group end. riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernel builds passed.
7532c8312f6af709e5689bf130f74d7c66914e6c:
fix(proc): return the thread id from set_tid_address

Linux set_tid_address returns the caller's thread id, not the thread-group id. Return sys_gettid() after recording clear_child_tid so pthread runtimes see the TID they registered.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 musl libctest hangs at pthread_cancel_points after 14 completed entries in .kernel-build/test-runs/20260509-154048-full/logs/riscv64-musl-libctest.log. Before implementation returned sys_getpid(); after implementation returns sys_gettid().

Build validation passed: make ARCH=riscv64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, make ARCH=loongarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only, make ARCH=aarch64 BRINGUP=1 kernel-only.

proc: reject setsid from process group leaders

Linux requires setsid to fail with EPERM when the caller is already a process group leader. Add that guard before assigning a new session and process group.

Focused before/after probe: /bin/setsid_probe after setpgid(0,0) changed from setsid=4 errno=0 to setsid=-1 errno=1. Kernel-only builds passed for riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64.

Reject invalid clone3 argument sizes, Linux-invalid clone flag combinations, mismatched stack pointer/size fields, and bad CLONE_PIDFD user pointers before creating a task.

Focused riscv64 glibc LTP clone302 before: 4 passed / 3 failed / 1 broken, with extra-size, sighand-no-VM, and thread-no-sighand unexpectedly succeeding before the test timed out. After: clone302 reports 12 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Builds passed: riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 kernel-only.

proc: support pidfd signal delivery

Create pidfd anonymous files for clone3(CLONE_PIDFD), implement pidfd_send_signal through the existing signal permission and delivery paths, and preserve queued siginfo payloads when building user signal frames.

Focused riscv64 glibc LTP clone301 before: 4 passed / 2 failed with pidfd_send_signal ENOSYS and missing child signal. After: 7 passed / 0 failed, including SIGUSR1 delivery and si_value 777. Builds passed: riscv64 dev-build, loongarch64 kernel-only, aarch64 kernel-only.

sched: reject invalid priority policies

Return EINVAL from sched_get_priority_min/max for unsupported scheduler policies instead of reporting zero priority bounds.

Focused before/after probe: /bin/sprio kept SCHED_OTHER at max=0 min=0 and SCHED_FIFO at max=99 min=1, while invalid policy 999 changed from max=0/min=0 errno=0 to max=-1/min=-1 errno=22. RISC-V focused run powered off cleanly; riscv64, loongarch64, and aarch64 bringup kernel-only builds passed.

futex: Preserve waiters on robust owner death

When processing a robust futex on thread exit, clear the dead TID and preserve FUTEX_WAITERS while setting FUTEX_OWNER_DIED. Leaving the dead TID in place and dropping waiters produced a non-Linux owner-death word for pthread robust mutex recovery.

The current tree already completes that focused libcbench run through group end in .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter5-libcbench-thread/before-riscv64-glibc-libcbench.log, so this iteration used a narrower robust-futex probe.

After: .kernel-build/agentloop/manual-tests/iter5-libcbench-thread/after-riscv64-robust-owner.log reported robust_word=0xc0000000 expected=0xc0000000 status=0x0.

Under focused riscv64 musl cyclictest stress, forced OOM pressure previously selected pid 2 user, pid 3 mksh, and pid 4 sh before benchmark workers. Validate nanosleep requests by rejecting tv_nsec >= 1s and round nonzero sub-tick sleeps up to one scheduler tick, matching the POSIX timer conversion used by clock_nanosleep absolute sleeps.

Baseline evidence: riscv64 glibc LTP clock_nanosleep01 passed 3 invalid-argument checks, then timed out in SEND_SIGINT. feat(live2d_load): keep the frame cache out of the 8kib QEMU build

Merging the WS2812 work pushed the QEMU variant over its SRAM limit —
`arm-none-eabi-ld: STM32 SRAM overflow`, bss 8333 B against an 8192 B part.
check-stm32f103 did not catch it because it only links the 512K/64K xuanwu
firmware, not the 8K QEMU one.

The frame cache needs SDIO to read from and external SRAM to cache into, and
QEMU's stm32vldiscovery models neither, so all of it was dead weight there —
1152 B of which was the band buffer alone. Guard it on !CONFIG_STM32_QEMU.

The band buffer could not be guarded before because live2d_load_draw_fs()
referenced it from outside the hardware ifdefs. That function — the uncached
"read the frame straight from SD and blit it" path — has had no callers since
the prefetch cache replaced it, so it goes too.

bss 8333 -> 7116 B. QEMU self-test runs again, including the new
`rgb-matrix: 5x5 framebuffer PASS`.
3320be30b2b2573a713970ea8ebbdc03525b1fb0:
fix(ir): decode NEC from edge intervals instead of busy-waiting in the ISR

The EXTI9 handler measured every high pulse by spinning, ~60ms per frame. That
starved the 9600-baud USART RX (a byte is 1ms, so a frame could eat ~60 of
them) and it was what overran SDIO's polled FIFO in §4o, until the data phase
started masking interrupts. Ambient IR from fluorescent light triggers spurious
edges, so the cost was paid with no remote in the room. It also timed those
pulses with a calibrated nop loop — the same unreliable pattern §4l had to
remove from DHT11; at 72MHz its "20us" unit was a guess and the thresholds
drifted with it.

No timer capture needed: NEC puts its information in the gaps between falling
edges (leader 13.5ms, '0' 1.125ms, '1' 2.25ms), so the handler is now a DWT
timestamp, a subtraction and a compare. An out-of-spec gap drops the partial
frame rather than shifting in a wrong bit, since a corrupted code would
dispatch a real action.

Adds an `ir` command (edges/frames/aborts). A high edge count with zero frames
means the receiver is seeing noise, not that decoding broke — previously
indistinguishable.

wifi: recover the IP when the module joined behind our back

The ESP8266 keeps the last AP in its own flash and rejoins at power-on,
announcing WIFI GOT IP without the firmware issuing CWJAP. That async path set
got_ip but never ran CIFSR, so `wifi` reported "ip=(none)" while the proxy
socket was plainly working. Ask once per connection when the state machine is
idle; the flag stops a failed query re-arming every service pass. Also report
"(module-remembered)" rather than "(not-configured)" for the SSID in that case
— the firmware genuinely does not know the name, and the old label read as a
fault.

Both verified on hardware.

docs: rewrite §5 as the resume-here entry point

M0-M5 are all board-verified now, so §5 becomes "current state vs remaining
work", separating what has real hardware evidence from what has only been
compiled. Records the WS2812 investigation: the software side is ruled out with
reasons (pin matches the vendor example, no PE5 contention, timing within spec,
DWT verified live), so the next person doesn't redo it — and notes that
`update=ok` is not evidence the LEDs received anything, since WS2812 has no
readback. Flags that the merged "CN5 short 5V-E5V" claim contradicts the board.

f52f441f844fa2fe35ab5a0ff15331a72b11869e:
refactor(mm): move VMO into core and back native VMAR with core mmap helpers

VMO becomes a core page source (mm/vmo.c): frames are owned by the VMO and
mapped through VM_VMO VMAs created by mm_mmap_vmo(), so demand faults
materialize pages on first touch and fork shares canonical frames instead of
copy-on-writing them. The Native VMAR layer is reduced to a thin wrapper over
mm_mmap_vmo/mm_munmap/mm_mprotect (abi/native/vmar.c), which removes the
silent truncation on partial page-allocation failure and fixes the frame
ownership bug where unmapping a VMO mapping double-freed its frames. Native
FILE/DEVICE mappings now go through mm_mmap_file and the page cache instead of
eager-loading into an anonymous VMO. The core fault path no longer includes
any ABI header.

the $I30 index root and index allocation blocks, and file read/write with

bf35c543c14149fad190425595179df2eec41afc:
feat(usb): add USB core XHCI host controller and HID class driver

Introduce a generic USB subsystem (drivers/usb/core, host, class):
- USB core: usb_device/interface/endpoint model, URB abstraction, the 'usb'
  bus that binds class drivers by class/subclass/protocol, and the port
  enumeration sequence driven by usb_hcd_ops.
- XHCI HCD: refactored from xhci_hid.c into an instance-based driver matched
  by the xHCI PCI programming interface.  Controller DMA structures are now
  allocated with explicit 64-byte alignment (kmalloc only guarantees 8/16),
  which fixes ring/context misalignment on QEMU; the CNR bit and event-ring
  setup follow the proven sequence.  USB 1.1 boot-protocol keyboard and mouse
  are supported through the usb-hid class driver.
- Enumeration is deferred to usb_core_scan() after driver_probe_all() so

554edfb1b87872149fde4137ee7ccaa39a3175d9:
refactor(sched): replace the MLFQ with an EEVDF proportional-share core

Replace the 8-level MLFQ for normal tasks with Earliest-Eligible-Virtual-
Deadline-First ordering. RT tasks keep the fixed-priority FIFO/RR class on
runqueue level 0 and always run ahead of the EEVDF list on level 1.

- Each normal task accumulates a weighted virtual run time
  (vruntime += dt * NICE0 / weight) and a virtual deadline
  (vruntime + virtual slice); the runqueue is kept sorted by deadline and
  the earliest is picked, so weight (nice) now actually controls CPU share.
- Fix the inverted nice->weight table (was stored smallest-weight-first,
  making nice decorative in the old level scheduler).
- Preemption and keep-current decisions compare virtual deadlines;
  wakeup preemption uses the same comparison.
- Accounting is charged on tick, yield, and context switch; a task's
  vruntime is preserved across sleep (sleeper bonus / latency friendliness).
- The aging scan and level demotion are removed (EEVDF lag guarantees
  progress without a starvation timer).

Two latent bugs surfaced by the new scheduling timing and fixed:
- user/Makefile: the find-based cmds compile rule dropped its source
  dependency, so user commands were never rebuilt after editing (also
  reverted to subdir-mirrored objects with proper pattern rules).
- vfs/procfs: a failed vnode open returned a blanket -ENOMEM, losing the
  specific error (e.g. -ESRCH when reading /proc/<pid>/maps after the task
  exits); propagate via task->vfs_open_errno.

Verified: dual-arch builds, riscv64 8-core sched_stress (smp-runqueue +
lock-split PASS), a nice probe showing nice -20 gets ~10000x the CPU of
nice 19, procfs/sched/futex/proc/mm/vfs stress, and all 21 gates.
da1e6b9f4420b9af29d39d1f6e31984b2cb94ea6:
feat(arch): add idle-task stealing for SMP load balance phase b

When a CPU's local EEVDF runqueue is empty, pull a runnable task from a
remote CPU so idle cores absorb bursty wakeups (e.g. Cargo spawning many
compiler threads) instead of idling while other cores stay overloaded.

- Steal only a genuine surplus (remote nr_running >= 2), so a deliberately
  placed single task is never yanked off its CPU.
- Steal only EEVDF (normal) tasks; RT tasks are deliberately placed by the
  wakeup path and keep deterministic placement / sched_setaffinity.
- Respect the task's cpus_allowed: only steal when the local CPU is in its
  allowed mask.
- Use a non-blocking trylock on the remote runqueue (added
  spin_trylock_irqsave) so an idle CPU never waits on a busy one; the local
  runqueue lock is held throughout and the runqueue reference is transferred
  without a put/get gap.

8-core sched_stress smp-runqueue + lock-split PASS; all 1-core smokes and

  aggregate rate dt*NICE0/total_weight; a task is eligible only while
  vruntime <= vtime.  The pick now selects the earliest virtual deadline
  among eligible tasks, so an over-run task cannot be picked merely by
  having a short slice (completes the EEVDF model).
- Clamp the sleeper bonus to EEVDF_MAX_LAG on enqueue, so a task that
  sleeps for a long time cannot then hog the CPU.
- Add a global base-slice knob writable via /proc/a20/sched_base_slice
  (ms).  Short slices favor latency (desktop), long slices favor
  throughput/cache (HPC batch); eeVDF's deadline ordering applies it.

nice -20 vs 19 still shows ~100000x CPU share, and the knob reads/writes

43f77cf1f34c87a5d5caba5aa85ecc4939c9cbd2:
fix(ppc64le): fix task switch PTE user bits and radix process-table walk

- __switch: allocate the outgoing task_context_t below the current C stack
  so its r21 slot no longer overlaps the context_switch frame's LR save
  slot (the resume previously returned to the __switch continuation and
  jumped to 0).
- PTE encoding: move PTE_U to a software bit (49) and PTE_PRIV to bit 59.
  Bit 59 is the hardware EAA_PRIV after the byte swap, so user pages were
  accidentally marked privileged and their own .text faulted on fetch.
- Radix process table: stop byte-swapping the prtbe; QEMU reads the table
  with ldq_phys (little-endian), so a plain (root_pa & RPDB) | 13 entry now
  yields the correct walk base (previously corrupted to a bogus address,
  causing NOPTE on every user page).
- 0x500 storage-fault re-route: recover the user PC (ppc64_rtu_nip), r1 and
  r2 anchors that QEMU 10.0.11 clobbers when delivering a page fault to the
  external vector, and correct ctx->nip so __return_to_user reloads it.
- handle_present_page_fault: set PTE_A so radix R/C faults do not recur;
  ppc64 TLB page flush falls back to the full IS-form tlbie.
- Docs: record the pSeries/XIVE bring-up state and the above root causes.

The ppc64le user task now runs and its demand paging works; the shell is
not reached yet (residual 0x500 SRR0/nip corruption).
65fcbff14b45e1c5b53b2f18039e8ca6db9f3e79:
fix(ppc64le): fix radix PTE prtbe byte order and eager-map executable text

qemu-system-ppc64 compiles the ppc64 target big-endian, so every physical
table load (ldq_phys -> ldq_be_p) reads the process table and the radix
page tables big-endian.  The bootstrap installs them with stdbrx, but the
C runtime stored the values little-endian, so QEMU decoded garbage:

- Process table entry: the C store must byte-swap the architectural prtbe
  ((root & RPDB) | 13 | 0x40000000000000a0) so the memory bytes are the BE
  image, exactly like the PID0 entry from entry.S.  The RTS bits decode to
  52 (PRTBE_R_GET_RTS) and the root nls is 13 in the RPDS field.
- PTE values: arch_pte_from_pa and the flag layout were already the
  byte-swap image; PTE_PRIV (EAA_PRIV bit3) and PTE_COW (SW bit11) were in
  the wrong stored positions.  Keep the bswap-based encoding and fix the two
  flags plus arch_pte_addr decoding.

Also eagerly map executable file-backed pages at exec time on ppc64le: an
instruction storage fault is delivered to the external vector with SRR0
clobbered to the trap-entry address, so the faulting EA is unrecoverable and
demand paging never maps the code page (the user task stuck at the first
cross-page branch).  Eager text mapping eliminates code-fetch faults; data
faults keep DAR and demand paging works.

With these fixes the init process reaches "mksh main starting!".
d815553341aa5d32558eba05a7e9c96a335333d5:
fix(mm): allow MAP_FIXED mappings to shadow the brk heap

A MAP_FIXED anonymous mmap inside the brk range (musl mallocng reserves a
PROT_NONE guard page right below the metadata area) is handled by the brk
demand-fault path first because the page falls in [start_brk, brk).  That
mapped the guard page as an ordinary read/write brk page, silently
defeating its PROT_NONE purpose and letting a heap underflow corrupt data.

Only take the brk path when the page is not already covered by a VMA (the
brk VMA is itself installed by mm_brk, so untouched heap pages still go
through it; the anon VMA path maps them identically).  Pages carved out by
an mmap now resolve to that VMA and honour its protection, so the guard
page faults on access as intended.

proc_park_commit_donate mirrors park_commit but, when the target is
fully parked on the same CPU, hands the CPU directly to it with a
dispatch reference instead of queueing in the runqueue (L4-style
donation; depth is implicitly one since the donor is BLOCKED). The
channel_call send stage defers the RECV wake (a20_channel_send_dwc) so
the server stays donatable; the reply wait (recv_begin_donate) either
donates or issues the deferred wake and parks normally, preserving
full typed-channel and race semantics. Measured RPC ping-pong on TCG:
83-84 vs legacy send+recv (~16-17% faster; previously 102-104),
smp=4 consistent, full smoke battery and loongarch64 build green.

A well-known registry channel pair is created at boot; the client
endpoint is installed into every native task's start_info
(service_registry) on both exec and task_spawn paths, and the server
endpoint is claimed by the supervisor via registry_claim (ownership
auto-released before the EXITED event fires). svcmgr spawns services
from a manifest, serves name lookups by transferring the service
endpoint as a channel-carried handle, and respawns crashed services
with fresh endpoints. The e2e client is an arbitrary process that
resolves rtcd by name, RPCs it, crashes it, and re-resolves after the
supervisor heals: smoke-native-registry passes, plus the full battery
and ABI=linux build (call sites guarded for native-only code).

ea8a06551d92d150ff1489ff8a3c1e4e81282a08:
fix(arch): fix SMP channel bulk corruption and VMA locking M5 follow-up

Root causes found and fixed for the SMP=8 channel bulk corruption
([SLAB BUG] kfree in a20_channel_recv_finish) seen in the 16MiB
native-shmring path:

1. Handle table shared storage with Linux ABI I/O scratch buffer:
   exec/startup stored the Native ABI handle table in task->scratch_buf,
   which proc_scratch_buffer() reuses for Linux I/O buffers; a Native
   task doing Linux-ABI I/O would kfree(ht) or write data into the
   handle table.  Added a dedicated task->a20_ht field; exec releases
   the pre-exec table on ABI transitions; exit cleanup releases ht and
   scratch_buf independently.

2. VMA list mutations ran without mm->lock while fault handling walked
   the list under the lock, so SMP mmap/munmap could tear the list
   (vma=<none> faults, PTE/chain corruption).  Split mm_mmap /
   mm_mmap_file / mm_mmap_vmo / mm_munmap / mm_mprotect / mm_mremap /
   mm_brk into _locked variants with locking wrappers; proc_brk /
   proc_mmap / proc_munmap now call the _locked variants.

3. Remote TLB flush deadlock: SBI REMOTE SFENCE.VMA is unreliable
   under QEMU TCG, and flushing remote TLBs while holding mm->lock
   (IRQs off) deadlocked both CPUs.  Replaced with IPI-based remote
   flush (pending bit + generation, spin with IRQs enabled), and
   deferred all remote flushes until after mm->lock is dropped
   (wrapper + trap-return paths; fault paths flush locally in-lock and
   publish remotely at trap return; mm_destroy and brk shrink publish
   a full remote flush).  VMA release (vfs_close may do block I/O) is
   deferred via mm->deferred_vma and flushed after unlock.

Diagnostics kept: always-on spinlock owner tracking + LOCK-STALL print,
buddy double-allocation/double-push detection, big-alloc canary,
channel trace ring, pfa.meta boot print.  SMP=2/8 native-shmring PASS
rate improved from 0% to majority; residual occasional channel double
free under heavy load is still under investigation.

e745354d630ac4c75835f8ca67358d8df741be21:
fix(mm): fix buddy allocator re-entry and TLB release ordering

Follow-up fixes for the remaining SMP channel/ring corruption:

1. Buddy allocator: releasing an order>0 block whose interior frames were
   still referenced (separate refcounts via COW/VMO mappings) pushed the
   whole dirty block back onto the free list; a later allocation handed out
   in-use frames (double allocation) and the VMO memset clobbered user
   pages.  fl_push_clean() now splits dirty blocks and only pushes clean
   sub-blocks; DIRTY-SPLIT diagnostics guard the split path.

2. Page-release TLB ordering: mm_destroy() and vmo_destroy() released
   frames before flushing remote TLBs, so another CPU could allocate a
   just-freed frame and be corrupted through a residual TLB entry.  Flush
   now happens BEFORE frames return to the buddy; oom swap reclaim also
   publishes a full remote flush after unlocking.

3. a20_channel ch_try_enqueue() took no peer reference (the park path
   does), so a concurrent ep_release() could free the peer under an
   in-flight enqueue; enqueue now pins the peer with refcount_inc_not_zero
   and releases it on every exit.

4. Diagnostics: frame release trace (frame_trace_dump_pfn), VMO frame
   content probe, RISCV64 IPI TLB flush call/service counters, kernel-
   address fault leak print.  All validated: IPI TLB flush is fully
   serviced (597/598 observed).

feat(net): add socket proxy transport

Third milestone of the network-stack migration: AF_INET sockets created
while the frame plane is active are proxied to the userspace netd service
(userspace lwIP), which owns the TCP/UDP connection state.

Kernel side (net/netd_sock.c + net/netd_sock_proxy.h):
- netd registers a pool of RPC channel endpoints (A20_SYS_netd_sock_register);
  each proxied socket gets its own channel so request/reply pairing is
  trivial and blocking ops (accept/connect/recv) park on the reply.
- net_socket_create/net_bind/net_listen/net_accept/net_connect/net_sendto/
  net_recvfrom/net_getsockname/net_getpeername/net_setsockopt/net_poll_events/
  close dispatch to the proxy when s->netd_id >= 0; accepted sockets carry
  the netd connection id into a fresh kernel socket object.
- TX frames go through A20_SYS_netd_tx_send: the kernel copies the frame
  and enqueues it into the TX ring with per-page VMO copies (userspace
  shared-memory writes are not reliably visible to the kernel with the
  current VMO mapping semantics).

netd side (user/svc/netd_sock.c):
- lwIP TCP/UDP connection table, tcp_accept/tcp_recv/tcp_err callbacks,
  pending accept/recv replies (blocking ops held until the condition is
  met), and the RPC service loop that dispatches by h->id (accepted
  children share the listener's channel).

Fix list along the way:
- VMO pages are not physically contiguous: ring slots and TX headers are
  reached via per-page pfn lookup (netd_vmo_poke/peek) instead of linear
  pfn_to_virt indexing.
- netd maps the ring VMO at a fixed low hint (0x10000000) so the ring pages
  never collide with the 0x60000000 mmap arena (anonymous VMA shadowing
  would have swallowed the VMO faults).
- netd_frame_ring data[] gets explicit size so the RX and TX ring data
  regions do not overlap each other's headers.
- netif must be marked up (netif_set_up) before lwIP accepts IP packets.
- userspace ring_write cursor math fixed (producer writes head slot and
  advances head).
- vmar VMO mappings switched from MAP_PRIVATE to MAP_SHARED.

TCP handshake completes (SYN-ACK leaves through the frame plane), accept
callback fires, and the kernel socket proxy round-trips create/bind/listen.

under debug (handshake/accept green, echo data not yet returned).

refactor(drivers): separate driver deployment from architecture setup

profiles: generic links only the unified driver core, buses and kernel
services, with every discoverable device driver packaged as a .a20drv
module loaded from the Early (/boot/drivers) or Runtime (/bin/lib/drivers)
DriverStore; embedded statically links the complete driver set (ppc64le and
armv7m default to embedded because they lack a drvmod toolchain).  AHCI,
DW SDIO and virtio-scsi join virtio-blk and RTC in the Early DriverStore so
root-device bootstrap no longer needs built-in drivers.

- driver core: busless devices no longer match drivers by wildcard; a
  busless driver must accept the device via an explicit match() callback.
  Board devices (VF2 SDIO/GMAC, LS2K1000 GMAC) register on platform_bus
  with a hardware_id; UART matches by name.  Fix drv_priv base
  initialization in the dw-sdio/starfive-gmac/ls2k-gmac class ops.
- drvmod loader: apply each RELA section against its own target section
  (.rela.rodata was swallowed by a strstr ".data" match); place .lbss/.ldata
  (x86 large model); fix LoongArch GOT_PC_LO12 to use the unscaled byte
  offset; aarch64 modules build with -mno-outline-atomics; module size
  limit raised to 512 KiB (virtio-net needs ~300 KiB of aligned BSS);
  descriptor type check covers RTC..USB; pinned modules are not re-entered
  by later DriverStore scans; add missing exports (pfa, clock_get_ticks,
  gpu_device_*, usb_*, a20_lwip_*, arch_virtio_net_probe).
- arch boundary: Linux ptrace register layouts, drvmod MMIO window limits
  and the Early DriverStore overlay tables move to kernel/arch/<arch>/;
  common code carries no CONFIG_<arch> branches (check-arch-boundary).
  Remove the duplicate arch_tlb_flush_page_local left in riscv32/ppc64le
  by the earlier TLB cleanup.

  virtio_blk_get_dev(); ppc64le board keeps its RTAS virtio probes via the
  embedded profile.

7006ab349ad67c07aa8c871341a15c1be0273e4d:
feat(net): implement SCM_CREDENTIALS SO_PASSCRED and SO_PEERCRED

D-Bus (and the GTK/XFCE stack that depends on it) authenticates clients
over AF_UNIX by requesting the peer credentials: the daemon sets
SO_PASSCRED and reads SCM_CREDENTIALS on recvmsg, and/or reads
SO_PEERCRED.  A20OS previously had SCM_RIGHTS only, so D-Bus would fail
its auth handshake with EOPNOTSUPP.

Add the credential plumbing across the unix-socket data path:

- net_msg_t / net_recv_meta_t carry sender pid/uid/gid; the enqueue path
  captures them from the sending task and the dequeue path forwards them.
- net_socket_t gains passcred plus peer_pid/uid/gid; the connect, accept
  and socketpair paths record the peer credentials for SO_PEERCRED.
- The channel-backed data plane (AF_UNIX socketpair/connect, which
  bypasses the legacy net_msg queue) records the latest sender in
  unix_ch_send and surfaces it on recvmsg when SO_PASSCRED is set.
- sendmsg accepts SCM_CREDENTIALS cmsgs (shape-validated) but records
  the real sending process credentials, matching Linux semantics.
- setsockopt/getsockopt gain SO_PASSCRED / SO_PEERCRED.

The SCM_STRESS user test now also verifies the credential round-trip and
peer-cred agreement.  All six architectures build; smoke-scm-stress,
smoke-syscall-ext, smoke-proc-stress, smoke-futex-stress and
smoke-vfs-stress pass.

feat(drm): implement KMS ioctls and PRIME buffer sharing

labwc's wlroots DRM backend needs a fuller KMS/PRIME surface than the
existing virtio-gpu DRM driver provided.  This completes it:

  implement DRM_IOCTL_MODE_OBJ_GETPROPERTIES (returning an empty set);
- implement DRM_IOCTL_GET_MAGIC/AUTH_MAGIC/SET_MASTER/DROP_MASTER with a
  per-open master flag so libseat can take DRM master;
- implement DRM_IOCTL_MODE_ADDFB2 (wlroots always uses it);
- implement DRM_IOCTL_PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD/FD_TO_HANDLE backed by a memfd
  snapshot of the dumb buffer, with a global fd<->handle table because
  wlroots exports on one open and imports on another;
- make dumb buffers global to the device (Linux semantics) so a handle
  created by the allocator open is visible to the backend open;
- give /dev/dri/card0 the standard Linux DRM major (226) so libdrm can
  classify the node, and implement a proper mmap path (sys_mmap routes
  /dev/dri/card0 mmaps through drm_linux_mmap which maps the buffer VMO,
  returning a page-aligned fake offset from MAP_DUMB).

as an FB, and commit frames; labwc now renders on virtio-gpu-gl.

feat(drivers): complete VIRTIO block I/O on interrupts and retry after queue reset

Register an IRQ handler as the primary completion path (ack ISR, drain
used ring, wake parked waiters) and keep polling only as the fallback
for IRQ-less transports.  A timed-out request now fails in-flight I/O,
resets and re-initialises the device on the existing DMA buffers, and
lets the rw-level retry loop resubmit instead of permanently fencing
off the disk.  A single 10 s write timeout during ext4 JBD2 recovery
previously disabled the device, refused the evaluator rootfs mount and
zeroed the whole run.  Timeout budget raised to 30 s.
4a8702f43d57be6349f955a4abda3e1b60a24182:
fix(fs): mount ext4 with deferred journal cleanup on flush failure

A timed-out VirtIO write during JBD2 recovery previously refused the
/mnt mount and zeroed the whole release-eval run.  Journal replay now
stays in the block cache and the mount continues when the device
rejects the flush; the on-disk journal is left untouched, so the next
mount replays it idempotently and any partially flushed prefix stays
consistent.  Cleanup after a successful replay (mark_empty, clearing
the recover flag) degrades the same way.

bcache adds a 30 s write quarantine after a failed device write: sync
fails fast instead of paying the driver retry budget per dirty entry,
and eviction prefers clean victims while the device is known-wedged.
bcache_sync_checked now also aborts on the first error rather than
multiplying the stall across every remaining dirty entry.

1a43d44088645379b6b124360cc053333abb7e7e:
feat(abi): implement splice tee and vmsplice in the kernel

splice(2)/tee(2)/vmsplice(2) previously delegated to copy_file_range,
which fails on pipes (-ESPIPE) and made tee consume its source.  Add a
core engine (kernel/fs/splice.c) that operates on vfile objects:

- file->pipe, pipe->file, and pipe->pipe transfers via a copy loop with
  the existing blocking/non-blocking pipe machinery
- tee duplicates pipe->pipe without consuming the source (new pipe_peek
  primitive in kernel/fs/pipe.c)
- vmsplice copies user iov segments into a pipe; the fd must be a pipe
- offset semantics match Linux: explicit offsets are advanced, NULL
  offsets use and advance the file position; offsets on a pipe return
  -ESPIPE; no pipe endpoint returns -EINVAL
- SPLICE_F_MOVE/NONBLOCK/MORE/GIFT validation in the ABI wrapper;
  SPLICE_F_NONBLOCK controls the pipe side independently of O_NONBLOCK

Copy-based transfer matches Linux's own fallback for non-page-aligned
paths.
b133a3e27d9da94eae799075858766368476f8f1:
feat(abi): implement membarrier commands with cross-CPU barriers

membarrier(2) previously returned fake success for every command except
QUERY (which advertised only itself).  Implement the full set:

- QUERY advertises GLOBAL/GLOBAL_EXPEDITED/REGISTER_GLOBAL_EXPEDITED/
  PRIVATE_EXPEDITED(+SYNC_CORE/RSEQ)/REGISTER_PRIVATE_EXPEDITED(+SYNC_CORE/RSEQ)
- PRIVATE_EXPEDITED requires per-mm registration first, else -EPERM;
  REGISTER_* commands set the per-mm bit
- the barrier itself is a real cross-CPU fence: smp_membarrier_sync_all
  issues a reschedule IPI to every online CPU and waits for the handler's
  acquire fence ack (generation-counted), so remote threads observe all
  prior stores; single-CPU builds collapse to a local SEQ_CST fence
- unknown commands and nonzero flags return -EINVAL

1aa0a494d8fe760e82ae70e5b25c975dea1245d1:
fix(abi): fix clone TLS arg order in syscall hook

Linux AArch64 selects CLONE_BACKWARDS, so the clone(2) wire order is
(flags, newsp, parent_tidptr, tls, child_tidptr): tls in register x3,
child_tidptr in x4.  musl's aarch64 clone.s already arranges exactly
this, matching the A20OS sys_clone(flags, stack, ptid, tls, ctid)
signature.

The aarch64 arch_adjust_clone_args hook copied the LoongArch arg[3] <-> arg[4]
swap, but LoongArch's clone.s emits (flags, stack, ptid, ctid, tls) and needs
it while aarch64 does not.  Applying the swap installed the child tidptr as
tpidr_el0, so musl's __pthread_self() resolved to a garbage pthread struct and
every pthread exited with a NULL self->prev/->next in __pthread_exit (SIGSEGV
at 0x10 on first thread exit, visible in test_userfaultfd / pthread_create on
aarch64).

Make the hook a no-op with an explanatory comment; verified with a minimal
pthread_create/join, syscall_ext (includes userfaultfd), and syscall_smoke on
aarch64 QEMU.

f99cec70fa42b1151eb7561bc2e0b7f8169777c8:
fix(mm): skip global shared-dirty harvest scan when vnode has no MAP_SHARED file mappings

mm_sync_shared_dirty_for_vnode() runs on every page-cache read() and
fsync().  It held proc_lock and walked every task, every VMA, and every
page table even when the target file had no MAP_SHARED file mappings at
all - the common case for compiler inputs read through the page cache.

Track a per-vnode shared_file_maps count updated at the same sites as the
VMA's vnode reference (mm_mmap_file_locked create, vma_ref_file copies for
fork/split/mremap, and vma_release_file/elf_discard_vmas/msync-unwind
teardown).  The read/fsync path now takes one acquire load and returns
immediately when no shared file VMA exists, eliminating the O(tasks x
VMAs x PTEs) scan and its proc_lock/mm lock serialization per read.
8f6b732038f72f9114defdd058f401c4d3ad764f:
fix(loongarch64): add user vdso so clock_gettime gettimeofday avoid full traps

rustc and LLVM call clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC/REALTIME) constantly;
on LoongArch64 every call previously paid the full 816-byte trap save and
restore (32 GPRs + 32 LSX vector registers + ~16 CSR ops).  This adds a
riscv64-style vDSO: a one-page image linked at vaddr 0 (p_offset ==
p_vaddr) exported through AT_SYSINFO_EHDR, plus the shared read-only vvar
page with a seqlock-protected realtime anchor.

The image materializes the vvar address with li.d (no text relocations),
reads rdtime.d, computes ns via mulh.du/mul 128-bit math, and falls back
to syscall 113/169 for unsupported clock ids.  musl loongarch64 enables
VDSO_USEFUL and matches the unversioned __vdso_clock_gettime symbol.

Build integration: VDSO_CC/objcopy flags and KERNEL_OBJ embedding are now
per-arch (riscv64 unchanged); loongarch64 uses elf64-loongarch.
d8e44db0ced54a33a8f4fe93066ced68313a6845:
perf(mm): limit COW TLB shootdowns to CPUs active in the address space

Every COW fault previously called arch_tlb_flush_page(), which on both
riscv64 and loongarch64 sends an SBI/IPI flush to every online CPU and
spin-waits for each remote ack - the single most expensive kernel
operation under the 8-way parallel rustc parallel-build workload.

Only CPUs currently running the faulting address space (mm->active_cpus,
maintained by mm_context_enter/leave) can hold the stale PTE.  Replace the
broadcast with mm_tlb_shootdown_page(): bump tlb_generation (so a CPU that
left the mm and re-enters flushes via mm_context_enter on ASID hardware),
publish with a barrier, then invalidate just the active CPUs.  The
faulting CPU already flushed the page locally inside the fault handler.
The old frame is only released after the targeted shootdown completes, so
the deferred-free invariant from the parallel-compile TLB fix is kept.

Validated with QEMU SMP boots: mm_stress (cow/fork/mremap/dontunmap
phases), futex_stress, proc_stress and vfs_stress all PASS on riscv64 and
loongarch64.
41cd881c71e7cb0a8a195f90d89242ba6b566f9a:
fix(futex): skip the page-table walk on PRIVATE wake requeue wake_op

futex_phys_key() does a 3-level page-table walk on every FUTEX_WAKE,
FUTEX_REQUEUE and FUTEX_WAKE_OP, but the physical address is only used to
match cross-process SHARED futexes.  cargo's jobserver and most libc locks
are PRIVATE, keyed only by (mm, vaddr); the physical key is pure overhead
for them.

Thread the FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG (0x80) from the syscall dispatch into the
wake-side handlers and pass pkey=0 when private.  A PRIVATE wake can only
match waiters in the same mm at the same address via (mm, vkey), so this
is exactly Linux's keying semantics - and it additionally prevents a
PRIVATE wake from ever matching a foreign mm by physical-page alias.

Validated: futex_stress (including the cross-process shared-wake case via
MAP_SHARED anonymous), sched_stress and proc_stress all PASS on riscv64
SMP4; both kernels build cleanly.
06f0c0a14b0a5e4eefaf81f451ccdd8c0d770f22:
perf(mm): batch deferred frame frees so munmap exit take pfa.lock once per chunk

Large munmaps and exec/exit teardown release thousands of frames through
mm_tlb_invalidate_finish's deferred-hold drain.  Each held frame was freed
with its own global pfa.lock acquisition plus IRQ save/restore, serializing
all vCPUs' frees during a build.

Extract frame_put's refcount-decrement-and-buddy-merge core into
frame_put_locked() (caller holds pfa.lock), keep frame_put() as the single
lock wrapper, and add frame_put_many() which takes the lock once for a
batch.  mm_tlb_invalidate_finish now collects deferred frame holds into
64-entry chunks and drains each chunk with one lock acquisition.  The
refcount and TLB-shootdown ordering semantics are unchanged: the frames are
only released here, after the remote invalidation completed.

Validated: mm_stress/proc_stress PASS on riscv64 SMP4 and futex/sched/proc
stress PASS on loongarch64 SMP4.
aac3ef13b7cfa63d7feca18f20265970b55300b0:
perf(fs): make namespace lookups take the metadata lock in read mode

The whole-filesystem metadata_lock was a single mutex serializing every
namespace operation on all 8 vCPUs; cold lookups (dcache misses on the
thousands of distinct files a build touches) queued behind each other and
behind every create/unlink.

ext4_lookup is read-only through the block cache and the independently
locked vnode cache (g_ext4_vcache_lock), so convert metadata_lock to an
rw_mutex and take it in read mode for lookups and write mode for all
mutations (create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename/link/symlink/truncate,
unlink-on-release and unmount).  Mutations stay mutually exclusive with
lookups, preserving the documented cache-remove ordering; the vnode-cache
lock ordering (metadata -> vcache) is unchanged, and no mutation path
calls ext4_lookup, so the rw_mutex cannot self-deadlock.

Validated on riscv64 SMP4: vfs_stress (ext4 hardlink/truncate/open-unlink
phases), vfs_edge, mm_stress and proc_stress all PASS; both kernels build
cleanly.
97b71be25dc7ceb331312919f64104c6248e0ee2:
feat(input): support udev and libinput device discovery

Four syscall/ABI gaps were keeping eudev's runtime rules and libinput's
udev backend from working:

- netlink uevents carried no SEQNUM, so every event got seqnum 0 and
  udevd's is_devpath_busy() misjudged the first queued event as busy
  (delaying_seqnum 0 == seqnum 0) - no worker was ever spawned.  Emit a
  globally increasing per-uevent SEQNUM.

- /dev/input/eventN was hard-coded to event0 only.  devfs now lists and
  resolves every published input class device, so /dev/input/event1+ exist
  and match the udev database.

- /sys/dev/char/<maj>:<min> is a directory (libdrm walks device/drm below
  it) but also answers readlink() with the class-device path (relative,
  matching Linux).  libudev's udev_device_new_from_devnum() resolves it and
  the syspath then equals the one an enumerate from /sys/class yields -
  libinput's evdev_device_have_same_syspath() compares them exactly and was
  rejecting every device.  vfs_readlinkat() now allows a vnode with a
  readlink op even when it is a directory.

- read()/write() wrote straight into/from user pages while a filesystem
  path held its offset lock; a page fault inside the locked region could
  re-enter the same read and self-deadlock (LOCK-STALL owner == waiter in
  sys_read).  Both now bounce through the kernel scratch buffer and copy
  with the lock released.  The LOCK-STALL reporter also prints a backtrace
  when owner == waiter so future recurrences are caught precisely.

Desktop verified: eudev persists ID_INPUT_* into /run/udev/data, libinput
reports 'Adding A20OS evdev mux' for event0/event1, labwc configures both,
DRM modesets and presents, XFCE autostart runs and xfconfd activates.

longer needs to start without input devices.  Clean the leftover
diagnostics out of the stage-2 init; the udev waits stay bounded.
0da3329596db0a3784bff2cf92e0a482b6c93fcd:
fix(sync): make mutex recursive and move user copies out of offset_lock

The intermittent desktop self-deadlock (LOCK-STALL owner == waiter in
sys_read/sys_write) was a recursive acquisition of vf->offset_lock: a
filesystem read/write path re-enters the same vfile (e.g. writeback, /proc
rendering) while the shared-offset mutex is already held by the same task.
The spinlock inside the mutex then spins forever with owner == waiter.

Two changes eliminate it:

- read_into_user/write_from_user now take the shared-offset lock around only
  the kernel-buffer transfer and release it before copy_to_user/copy_from_user,
  so a page fault on the user buffer can never happen inside the locked region
  (that fault could re-enter the file read and deadlock).
- mutex_lock/mutex_unlock track a per-owner depth and allow recursive
  acquisition by the same task instead of self-deadlocking.  This is the
  correct behaviour for offset_lock, which is legitimately re-entered by the
  same task.  mutex_trylock/init handle depth too.

procfs files skip offset_lock entirely (vfs_is_procfs_vfile): rendering
/proc/<pid>/fdinfo locks another vfile's offset_lock and must not run under
this one.

The LOCK-STALL self-deadlock reporter now prints a 32-frame backtrace plus
the IRQ state when owner == waiter, and the recursive-mutex path logs the
first few hits so recurrences stay observable.
b8697340a0927679648545ce95413a01dd4e396d:
feat(core): add spinlock contention telemetry with callsite attribution

proc_lock is the dominant remaining lock under SMP builds; before
splitting it the audit needs to attribute contention to exact call sites.
Add contended_acquires/contended_spins to spinlock_t (incremented only on
the contended path, so the uncontended fast path stays a single exchange),
a fixed lock registry (core/lock_counters.c) exposed at
/proc/a20/lock_contention, and an optional per-callsite sample table (hash
of the caller's return address, symbolized through kallsyms) that is
enabled for proc_lock.

The initial counter implementation accidentally changed spin_lock_at's
acquire loop from while(exchange) to if(exchange), letting a waiter fall
through without re-acquiring after the owner released the lock, so two
CPUs could enter the critical section together under SMP.  The loop is
restored to the original retry semantics with the counters preserved.

Registers: proc, runq (per-CPU), page_cache, dcache, block_cache,
vfile_table.  Contended-path cost is two relaxed atomic adds.
9d6f4fa31c17699804102cb02c8b9243e7721981:
perf(fs.page_cache): shard page-cache locks and add second-chance eviction

The single g_page_cache_lock serialized every buffered read and
page_cache_mark_dirty across eight parallel rustc processes.  Split the
262144 hash buckets into PAGE_CACHE_BUCKET_LOCKS=1024 independent
spinlocks; a warm hit now takes only its bucket lock, an atomic refcount
and an accessed bit, never touching the global lock or mutating the global
LRU.  Eviction uses second-chance (clock) approximation and re-checks the
refcount under the candidate's bucket lock so a concurrent hit can never
be pinned and reclaimed.

Lock ordering: a caller may hold g_page_cache_lock and then a bucket lock,
but never acquire the global lock while holding a bucket lock.  All
detach/invalidate/truncate paths take the bucket lock for hash
manipulation while holding the global lock.
a18702f6b3cbba82efa1d70813d6c6e593cdf727:
perf(fs.block_cache): shard cache locks and scope writeback

The per-mount bc->lock serialized every ext4 metadata and 4K-page access.
Both pools now hash into BCACHE_BUCKET_LOCKS=256 bucket locks; warm hits
take only the bucket lock, an atomic refcount and an accessed bit.
Evictors re-check the refcount under the candidate's bucket lock and use
second-chance LRU.

Also add bcache_sync_scoped(): flush only the listed dirty 4K pages (plus
any dirty 512-byte metadata blocks) under the same writeback_lock and
per-page dirty_gen ordering as a full sync, so one file's fsync no longer
writes back the whole mount's dirty block cache.
43d0466218c2cf64af905ac47b46cdea7f02de56:
perf(fs.vfs.dcache): shard dcache locks and add second-chance eviction

Every path component took the single g_dcache_lock.  Split the hash into
VFS_DCACHE_BUCKET_LOCKS=64 bucket locks; a hit takes only the bucket lock
and sets an accessed bit.  Slot allocation and the LRU stay under the
global lock but run only on insert/evict, and the evictor re-checks the
entry under its bucket lock so the vnode_get in a concurrent lookup is
atomic against slot reuse.
964f9556e9f7acc35456a80a6e1b3e295a115b46:
perf(fs): scope fsync to the inode instead of the whole mount

vfs_fsync previously called bcache_sync() on the entire mount, writing back
every concurrent writer's dirty data pages on each fsync.  Add
vnode_ops.sync_vnode and an ext4 implementation (ext4_vn_sync) that flushes
only this file's data extents, its inode-table page, and the bitmaps and
group descriptors of the block groups it occupies, via
bcache_sync_scoped().  Filesystems without the op fall back to the full
mount sync.

Crash durability for the file's data, inode and allocation bitmaps is
preserved; other files' data is left dirty for their own fsync, matching
Linux fsync(file) semantics (the parent directory entry is not guaranteed
durable either).
0e88144da7d909bd74bbdf662690c5ebbccbd3de:
perf(fs): reuse one scratch buffer across directory blocks

ext4_dir_find/add/remove/update_entry allocated a block-sized buffer per
directory block and freed it at the end of every iteration, putting each
cold directory miss on the shared slab lock.  Hoist the allocation to one
buffer per call and free it once.

A stray per-iteration kfree left over from the refactor freed the reused
buffer on the first block and then wrote through the dangling pointer,
causing a use-after-free and stale double-free under real SMP8; it is
removed so the single final kfree is the only release.
656da060f8ca66283f8e718601790db864e2daa8:
perf(proc): take proc_lock once per context switch

sched() acquired proc_lock for the current-vs-next preemption check, then
released it and context_switch() acquired it again to publish the on_cpu
transition, so every context switch paid the global lock twice.  Split
context_switch() into context_switch_locked() (assumes proc_lock is held
with the caller's irqsave flags and releases it at the same points) and a
thin wrapper; sched() now keeps the lock held across the publication.

Lock order is unchanged (proc_lock -> mm_struct.lock is documented and
mm_context_enter() only uses atomics), and holding the lock through the
whole publication closes the window where a remote observer could see the
selected task as neither selected nor owned.  SMP8 mm_stress measurement:
proc_lock contention dropped from 33335 contended / 16.2M spins to 16750 /
9.0M spins.
8d490bc111494bd90d87f9d6307dbb4801564bcc:
perf(fs): enlarge the sequential readahead window to 128 kib

The readahead burst and the demand-fault fault-around shared one 16-page
(64 KiB) constant.  Compiler inputs are read sequentially, so a separate
PAGE_CACHE_READAHEAD_PAGES=32 window lets ext4 merge one contiguous 128 KiB
block request instead of two 64 KiB round trips; the anonymous/file
fault-around stays at 16 pages to bound per-fault memory commitment.
92d33acd704226807ec9c926a3e8cdc69a64139a:
perf(proc): finish park wakeups without proc_lock

proc_park_finish() took proc_lock just to reset the woken task's park
fields.  Every wake path already cancelled the timer (proc_try_wake and the
timer expiry both reset wait_timer_index to -1), so the reset has no
concurrent writer once the task is running again and a stale wake on a
WOKEN/IDLE task is a no-op.  Skip proc_lock when no timer index is pending
and reset the fields with atomic stores; only a stale pending index falls
back to the heap lock.

SMP8 mm_stress measurement: proc_lock contended acquires dropped from a
16-30K range to 12-20K (median roughly 28K -> 16K).  An earlier attempt
that also removed the post-sched wake_reason read regressed contention
(the acquisition acted as a natural throttle on park/wake cycles), so that
piece was reverted; this commit keeps only the finish fast path.
4f08ae6ea493abeffd5034d3b534a28c46af98b8:
refactor(proc): split the park wake state machine to a per-task park_lock

proc_lock serialized every park/wake transition (prepare, commit, cancel,
interrupt, and the wake) plus the wait-timer heap, making it the dominant
remaining lock under SMP builds.  Give each task its own park_lock for the
PREPARING/PARKED/WOKEN state machine and give the wait-timer heap its own
lock, so the park path no longer touches proc_lock at all.

Lock order (proved acyclic): park_lock -> timer lock, park_lock -> runqueue
lock, and proc_lock -> park_lock (make_ready, exit waiters, wait4).  The
timer scan collects expired entries under the timer lock, releases it, then
wakes each target under its park_lock (never holding both).  The post-sched
wake_reason read in proc_park_commit keeps proc_lock deliberately: removing
it previously regressed contention because that acquisition throttled
park/wake cycles.

proc_wake_q_flush now wakes each queued task under its own park_lock
instead of one proc_lock for the whole batch.

SMP8 mm_stress: proc_lock contended acquires dropped from a 16-30K range
(baseline) to 8.7-19K (median roughly 28K -> 14K).  futex/proc/sched/vfs/mm
stress PASS on real SMP8; network suite is byte-identical to baseline.
b6a607bf4ae40a7633a907cb9c212017adc189f3:
fix(build): skip the LVGL desktop in text-mode dev builds

make run-riscv64 (and other text-mode dev-build consumers) compiled the
entire LVGL source tree into the desktop binary even though a -nographic
boot never launches it.  Gate the desktop on USER_BUILD_DESKTOP so only
GUI-targeted builds (run-gui-*, smoke-qemu-gui-*, VirtualBox ARM64 GUI
images) pay for it, and fold the flag into USER_BUILD_ID so text/GUI
builds never share a stamp or leak a stale desktop binary into an image.

4c00330871ec46e4ec61460d7e7b436614eba506:
fix(user): pad uc_sigmask to 128 bytes so uc_mcontext matches the Linux musl ucontext ABI

The kernel-side struct ucontext embedded a raw 8-byte sigset, placing
uc_mcontext at offset 48 (riscv64) / 56 (loongarch64).  The Linux ABI
pads the sigmask to the user-space sigset_t size (128 bytes), so musl
and glibc expect uc_mcontext at offset 176.  Signal handlers that modify
the saved context (qemu's SIGILL feature probes do 'uc->uc_mcontext.
gregs[REG_PC] += 4') wrote the advanced PC to offset 176, but rt_sigreturn
restored it from offset 48, silently discarding the change.  qemu's
cpuinfo_init probe then re-executed the illegal Zimop instruction forever
(riscv64 SIGILL storm) or corrupted the caller's stack canary
(loongarch64 'stack smashing detected').

Add the missing 120 bytes of padding so both arches place uc_mcontext
at 176, exactly matching musl's ucontext_t (verified by sizeof and
offsetof against the musl build used for the userland).

010c49c666eb65c713c776387c187dca635675eb:
fix(abi): bound syscall iov lengths and page counts

sys_sendmsg/sys_recvmsg summed up to 1024 user-controlled 64-bit iov
lengths into total with no overflow check: a wrapping total allocated a
tiny scratch buffer while the copy loop wrote full iov lengths past it
(kernel heap overflow). sys_move_pages multiplied nr_pages by sizeof(int)
without an overflow check (32-bit wrap) and silently ignored allocation
failure. sys_readv/sys_writev had no iovcnt cap, letting iovcnt=INT_MAX
force a ~2^31-iteration syscall.

- checked iov length accumulation (SIZE_MAX - total) in sendmsg/recvmsg
- checked nr_pages * sizeof(int) and return -ENOMEM on allocation failure
- cap readv/writev iovcnt at 1024 (matching sendmsg) and reject negative

32db7f0035dd97d03a1d1428a678389ec0d4e0a1:
fix(abi): reject overlong user paths with ENAMETOOLONG

user_strncpy() truncates at max-1 without signalling, so openat, truncate,
mkdirat, renameat2, linkat, symlinkat, mount/umount2, fspick, open_tree,
move_mount, mount_setattr, swapon/mkswap/swapoff, name_to_handle_at,
acct, execveat, inotify_add_watch, fstatat, statx, readlinkat, fchmodat,
utime(s)at and the xattr-at helpers silently operated on a wrong path
instead of failing like Linux.  Add user_path_strncpy() (copies a user
path and returns -ENAMETOOLONG when the kernel buffer fills without a
NUL) and switch every path syscall to it, matching the check sys_execve
already had.  Verified with make smoke-abi-linux.
3cde8b3a63cf3ffabe863a61bb57a4b2a66906c8:
fix(sched): skip proc_lock in switch completion without a pending handoff

proc_switch_complete() unconditionally took proc_lock even though
proc_switch_complete_locked() early-returns when nothing was published
for this CPU.  The slot is written only by the local CPU, so a NULL read
cannot race: early-return without the lock for the first boot switch and
for the case where a preempted incoming stack was already completed by
proc_set_current().  The common blocked-task switch still serializes on
proc_lock because the enqueue decision for a wake that raced the switch
must stay atomic with the waker (park protocol); a lock-free completion
would need a per-task wake-queue bit, deferred.

EEVDF: insert a freshly woken task in O(1) when its new virtual deadline
is later than every queued deadline (the common case), instead of walking
the sorted list on every wake.  Ties append, preserving the existing
equal-deadline ordering; the first-task path now links directly.
ea7d90bf0123f744f031d04c6a302432e0163ee6:
refactor(sched): replace SIGALRM task-list scan with a deadline min-heap

sched_scan_timers() walked the entire task list under proc_lock whenever
any timer deadline was due, even when no task had an ITIMER_REAL alarm.
Add a per-task alarm min-heap (same pattern as the wait-timer heap):
proc_set_alarm_expire() inserts/removes under g_alarm_timer_lock and each
entry holds a task reference; expiry pops only due entries in O(k log n)
and re-arms periodic intervals.  Task destruction removes its entry via
proc_alarm_cancel() (proc_lock -> alarm lock, no reverse order).

Also skip the wait4() waiter scan on every exit: a proc_lock-guarded
global count of tasks parked with waiting_for_child makes
proc_wake_child_waiters_locked() return in O(1) when nobody is waiting
(the common case), keeping the full scan only while a wait actually
blocks.  Verified: smoke-riscv64, smoke-sched-stress, smoke-proc-stress,
smoke-futex-stress PASS; in-guest 'sleep 1' still fires SIGALRM.
60f664cbf5dacce8bd224b0f9aef4cfdf2d790a9:
fix(kernel): fix io_pgetevents OOB read COW perf counter and all warnings

1eb2473f6439b3c197dcd81850c5d02a0e9ccb33:
fix(envelope): charge readv and writev against data budgets

Previously sys_writev/sys_readv charged ops and enforced direction but
passed bytes=0 to the mediator, allowing a single writev/readv call to
transfer unlimited data without touching the data_budget counter.
Plain read/write charged correctly; only the vectorized variants had
the gap.

Fix: when enveloped, walk the user iovec array once to sum total
transfer length, then pass it as the data charge.  Conservative
pre-charge -- denial fires before any partial transfer, preventing
over-consumption within a single call.

read/write/pread64/pwrite64 (bytes=count) and
writev/readv (bytes=sum of iov lens).

a92abf20822674d445361e8ab40e39fdfa9ac704:
fix(user): pad uc_sigmask to 128 bytes so uc_mcontext matches the Linux musl ucontext ABI

The kernel-side struct ucontext embedded a raw 8-byte sigset, placing
uc_mcontext at offset 48 (riscv64) / 56 (loongarch64).  The Linux ABI
pads the sigmask to the user-space sigset_t size (128 bytes), so musl
and glibc expect uc_mcontext at offset 176.  Signal handlers that modify
the saved context (qemu's SIGILL feature probes do 'uc->uc_mcontext.
gregs[REG_PC] += 4') wrote the advanced PC to offset 176, but rt_sigreturn
restored it from offset 48, silently discarding the change.  qemu's
cpuinfo_init probe then re-executed the illegal Zimop instruction forever
(riscv64 SIGILL storm) or corrupted the caller's stack canary
(loongarch64 'stack smashing detected').

Add the missing 120 bytes of padding so both arches place uc_mcontext
at 176, exactly matching musl's ucontext_t (verified by sizeof and
offsetof against the musl build used for the userland).

48b44eedd6670471d8e008a152b629111120b616:
fix(sched): skip proc_lock in switch completion without a pending handoff

proc_switch_complete() unconditionally took proc_lock even though
proc_switch_complete_locked() early-returns when nothing was published
for this CPU.  The slot is written only by the local CPU, so a NULL read
cannot race: early-return without the lock for the first boot switch and
for the case where a preempted incoming stack was already completed by
proc_set_current().  The common blocked-task switch still serializes on
proc_lock because the enqueue decision for a wake that raced the switch
must stay atomic with the waker (park protocol); a lock-free completion
would need a per-task wake-queue bit, deferred.

EEVDF: insert a freshly woken task in O(1) when its new virtual deadline
is later than every queued deadline (the common case), instead of walking
the sorted list on every wake.  Ties append, preserving the existing
equal-deadline ordering; the first-task path now links directly.
068871d7dcde6e7541d0dc9ed62dd65b735af9dc:
refactor(sched): replace SIGALRM task-list scan with a deadline min-heap

sched_scan_timers() walked the entire task list under proc_lock whenever
any timer deadline was due, even when no task had an ITIMER_REAL alarm.
Add a per-task alarm min-heap (same pattern as the wait-timer heap):
proc_set_alarm_expire() inserts/removes under g_alarm_timer_lock and each
entry holds a task reference; expiry pops only due entries in O(k log n)
and re-arms periodic intervals.  Task destruction removes its entry via
proc_alarm_cancel() (proc_lock -> alarm lock, no reverse order).

Also skip the wait4() waiter scan on every exit: a proc_lock-guarded
global count of tasks parked with waiting_for_child makes
proc_wake_child_waiters_locked() return in O(1) when nobody is waiting
(the common case), keeping the full scan only while a wait actually
blocks.  Verified: smoke-riscv64, smoke-sched-stress, smoke-proc-stress,
smoke-futex-stress PASS; in-guest 'sleep 1' still fires SIGALRM.

950e90bea965e7fa33cc0e511732eadd7b4b81c9:
fix(proc): link task_spawn/exec children into wait4 children list

The perf-core wait4 rewrite (f125fa7ff) scans the waiting thread
group's children lists instead of the global task table, but only
fork() populated those lists. Tasks created via the a20 task_spawn /
exec paths (proc_alloc, proc_alloc_user_image) were never linked, so
a20_task_wait on a spawned task returned -ECHILD while the child was
alive (NATIVE_ISOLATION: task_wait failed), and orphan reparenting
missed the same children.

under proc_lock, default tg_leader to self and link into the parent's
children list, mirroring fork.c.

Root cause of the flaky smoke-native-registry hang: the supervisor
and registry clients shared the service's client-facing endpoint
queue. svcmgr's pong reader drained that queue for health replies and
could consume a client's RPC reply (both are structurally identical
envelopes), leaving the client parked forever in channel_call.

Spawn now installs a second channel pair at A20_SVC_PING_SLOT;
ping/pong and the pong watch move to that endpoint, and svcmgr never
reads client_ep anymore. rtcd drains both endpoints (alarm replies
still go to the requesting endpoint), echod polls both, ufsd pumps
the ping endpoint. Documented the isolation in 01-mechanisms and
narrowed the known limitation in 02-mainstream-plan to genuine
multi-client concurrency.

interrupted syscall nr+args in a per-task restart block, and

handler table instead of leaking -ERESTARTNOINTR to userspace.  With
no pending restart the call returns -ENOSYS, matching Linux.  A pending
block is invalidated when any other syscall dispatches first.

wrong comparison class for every caller.  Align the mapping, add the
missing KCMP_EPOLL_TFD query over epoll membership by open-file
identity, gate both targets behind CAP_SYS_PTRACE or ptrace-style
access like pidfd_open, and return Linux's 0/1/2 ordering instead of a
binary equal/differ.

reports counters for that byte window through

is synchronous under the dirty-page owner, evicted counters are not
tracked per vnode.

page-aligned range inside one shared VM_FILE VMA, refuse sealed ranges,
pin the backing file across the transition, munmap the window and
re-enter it at pgoff*PAGE_SIZE through proc_mmap(MAP_SHARED|MAP_FIXED)

the creator's euid, mmap(2) refuses them to any other euid with -EACCES

kernel now writes cpu_id_start/cpu_id (current CPU), node_id 0 and
mm_cid through the direct map at registration and at every dispatch in
context_switch_locked, so sched_getcpu-style readers observe migrations.

alignment keeps the touched fields on one page.  Sequence-abort
delivery on preemption remains future work and is documented.

builds: a PROT_NONE guard page below a fresh anonymous RW mapping sized
up to page granularity, with SHADOW_STACK_SET_TOKEN demanding the top

returning the token slot as the initial SSP.  Non-x86 architectures
keep -ENOSYS, which is the arch-correct Linux behavior there.
5fbc0d017c6103fc4032ee47f78a386aa7717689:

Replace the synthetic "/" answer with a kernel dcookie registry:
producers register a (vnode, path) pair and hand out an opaque
generation-tagged cookie; SYS_lookup_dcookie resolves it back to the
recorded path with Linux's buffer semantics (required size when the
buffer is short, bytes-copied otherwise, -EINVAL for unknown cookies).

verifier (jump bounds, load offsets against seccomp_data, scratch
memwords, RET-only tail) and interpreter, per-task refcounted
newest-first filter chains inherited at fork, STRICT-mode syscall
whitelist, and a dispatch gate next to the KEP filter that applies

handling.  seccomp(GET_ACTION_AVAIL) reports the supported action set
and GET_NOTIF_SIZES returns real wire sizes; TSYNC, LOG flags and
USER_NOTIF are refused at install time rather than faked.  prctl gains
PR_SET_SECCOMP/PR_GET_SECCOMP.
7692145101709ea86998472e17e24415105d8e23:
feat(quota): implement quotactl and quotactl_fd with quota accounting

Replace the fixed -EOPNOTSUPP stubs with a quota subsystem: per-mount
per-type (USRQUOTA/GRPQUOTA) limit tables keyed by uid/gid carrying
byte and inode hard/soft limits plus live usage.  The VFS core feeds
it from real chokepoints -- write growth in vfs_write_file, ftruncate
growth, inode creation on O_CREAT/mkdir/symlink (caller credentials)
and unlink reclaim via the removed victim vnode -- enforcing EDQUOT on
exceeded hard limits.  quotactl implements Q_QUOTAON/OFF, Q_GETFMT,
Q_GETINFO/Q_SETINFO, Q_GETQUOTA/Q_SETQUOTA (CAP_SYS_ADMIN gated),

for the _fd variant, by the fd's own mount.
c64e4d99d5feb971fdaf1b7c63d4165cbfd5cdb2:
feat(kexec): stage kexec_load and connect reboot(KEXEC)

kexec_load no longer lies with a constant -EINVAL: user segments are
copied into freshly allocated frames (zero-filled to memsz), validated
against the kernel's physical extent derived through the direct map and
against each other, and staged atomically under the kexec lock with
rollback on partial failure.  kexec_file_load reads and ELF-magic-checks
the image and holds it for the architecture backend.  reboot(LINUX_
REBOOT_CMD_KEXEC) consults the staged state; until a machine_kexec MMU-
teardown trampoline exists per arch it returns -ENOSYS with an image
loaded and -EINVAL without one, mirroring Linux on backend-less boards.
KEXEC_CRASH/preserve-context flag variants are refused at load time.
