cd7a4794685ca67f10c57d7b99ba7783427f5609:
docs(roadmap): record that interleaved x86_64 A/B results were inconclusive

第一次在 x86_64/KVM 上真正做了交错 A/B(6 轮 x 2 臂 = 12 次运行，ON, OFF, ON, OFF, ... 严格交替，
两臂各用 EXTRA_CFLAGS=-DCONFIG_ANON_PROV_DEFAULT=4096 与 =0 预先构建好的内核，每轮先
cat /proc/a20/perf 预热计数器，再跑 cortenmm_bench mmap 1 与 cortenmm_bench mmap-pf 1)。

结果(中位数, ns)：
  mmap    high  ON 67046  OFF 65908  比值 1.017  离散 ON 45%/OFF 27%  p=0.873
  mmap    low   ON 77440  OFF 60206  比值 1.286  离散 ON 37%/OFF 20%  p=0.078
  mmap-PF high  ON 155551 OFF 151154 比值 1.029  离散 ON 34%/OFF 26%  p=0.873
  mmap-PF low   ON 158772 OFF 149132 比值 1.065  离散 ON 26%/OFF 29%  p=0.262
(Mann-Whitney 双侧正态近似，n=6/6。mmap low 原始值：ON [53675,79398,78493,63457,76387,82593]、
OFF [66425,55076,59134,54227,61277,62010]。)

结论必须写成「测不出来」：四个比较没有一个达到 p<0.05，最小的是 mmap low 的 p=0.078。更关键的
是组内离散度 20%-45%——同一臂自己六次运行的波动就已经大于绝大多数臂间差异。宿主是共享的
(taskset -c 12-15 只做了软绑定，没有独占核、没有裸金属)，这个噪声地板远高于本平台本应分辨的
<1.2x 效应。因此：关于 x86_64 上的预标记性能，本次不能下任何结论。既不能说「中性」，也不能说
「mmap 回归 29%」。

两条必须一并记录、但都不能当结论的观察：
1. mmap low 是唯一像有信号的一项(ON 慢 29%)，方向上与论文一致(SS6.2：预标记让 mmap 略慢)。但
   p=0.078、且两组原始值大幅重叠(ON 最低 53675 < OFF 最低 54227，ON 最高 82593 远超 OFF 最高
   66425)，6 个样本不足以支撑它。
2. mmap-PF 两项都是 ON 偏慢(1.029/1.065)，与论文预期的「mmap-PF 更快」方向相反；同样不显著，
   但方向相反这件事本身值得记住：它说明在这份噪声里，连方向都不可信。

两处方法学缺陷(如实记录)：
1. 这 12 份日志本身不能自证「ON 臂确实生效」——把 /proc/a20/perf 重定向到了 /dev/null。生效性
   是由产物同一性确立的：kern-4096.elf 与 §10.66 中实测 mm_anon_provisioned=9280 /
   mm_fault_from_status=2842 的那个构建是同一份，且两个 ELF 在第 542963 字节不同(正是预标记上
   限那个立即数所在处)。这个论证成立，但它不等于「日志自证」——下一轮务必把计数器打印进日志。
2. mm_stress 之外的基准未被纳入同一轮的对照，cortenmm_bench 的 low/high 两种模式各自的内存压力
   设定也未记录成文。

要真正分辨这个效应，需要的是降噪而不是加样本：
- 降噪，而不是加样本：独占核 / 裸金属 / 关掉同宿主其它负载。当前 20%-45% 的组内离散度下，把 n
  从 6 加到 60 也只是把噪声看得更清楚，不会让信号浮现。
- 改成进程内配对：在同一进程内交替 ON/OFF(需要运行时可切换——这正是 §10.69 认定「不做启动协议
  改造」时保留的那条路：用 a20.anonprov= 之类的运行时开关，就能在 x86_64 上做到这一点，从而把宿主
  漂移变成两臂共有的噪声)。这是当前最值得做的一步。
- 只有在拿到组内离散度降到个位数百分比的数据之后，才值得讨论 mmap / mmap-PF 的方向与幅度。

再次声明：在拿到这样的数据之前，不得在任何总结里写「x86_64 上预标记性能中性」或「mmap 回归
x%」。此前 §10.33/§10.34 那次 riscv64 上的「中性」结论只对 riscv64 成立，不能外推。
b0c5322e9e340eb6e84b1d5c8b53830e42090639:
feat(mm): add a runtime anonprov switch for paired tests within one boot

§10.70 判定「要降噪就得让两臂在同一进程内交替」，而此前唯一的开关是启动时的 cmdline/编译期
常量——这正是 §10.69 那个「启动协议改造」的真正用途。本轮用远小于启动协议改造的方式补上了它：把
上限暴露成一个可写 procfs 节点。

实现(kernel/mm/pt.c、kernel/include/mm/pt.h)：
- g_anon_prov_max 连同 mm_pt_anon_prov_max() / mm_pt_set_anon_prov_max() 移出
  #if defined(ARCH_HAS_PGTABLE_OPS) && !defined(CONFIG_NOMMU) 守卫——否则 NOMMU 链接时
  undefined reference(这个坑撞了两次才定位：先是访问器落在守卫内，再是变量本身也在守卫内)。它是
  不依赖页表的普通状态；NOMMU 下写它返回 -ENOSYS，读它照常返回当前值。
- 读用 __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE、写用 __ATOMIC_RELEASE：每次 mmap 都会读它，这个定序正是「一次启动内
  反复切换」能成立的前提。
接口(procfs)：PF_A20_ANONPROV，/proc/a20/anonprov，写入为十进制页数，范围 [0, 65536]，0 = 关闭。
读回与写入已实测：0 -> 写 4096 -> 4096 -> 写 0 -> 0。验证：5 架构 + riscv64/aarch64 NOMMU 构建
0 error。

单次启动内配对 A/B(8 轮，严格 ON/OFF 交替)：
  mmap    high  ON 61174  OFF 56398   1.085  离散 ON 21.3%/OFF 30.5%  p=0.248
  mmap    low   ON 62508  OFF 58542   1.068  离散 ON 50.0%/OFF 37.2%  p=0.318
  mmap-PF high  ON 140115 OFF 165997  0.844  离散 ON 43.3%/OFF 34.8%  p=0.093
  mmap-PF low   ON 146172 OFF 165292  0.884  离散 ON 32.0%/OFF 28.8%  p=0.074
本次日志自证了 ON 臂生效(补上了 §10.70 的方法学缺陷 1)：mm_anon_provisioned: 19467、
mm_fault_from_status: 8859。

两条结论，方向相反，都必须写下来：

(1) 我的降噪预期是错的。§10.70 断言「进程内配对能把宿主漂移变成两臂共有的噪声」——实测没有
发生：配对后的组内离散度是 21%-50%，与跨启动 A/B 的 20%-45% 基本相同，一点也没有降。mmap low
的 ON 离散甚至达到 50%。这说明主导噪声的不是「两臂之间的宿主漂移」，而是每次测量内部的宿主噪声
(同宿主其它负载抢占、cache 抖动、TCG/KVM 翻译缓冲抖动)，配对法原理上就治不了它。这条预期被
自己的实验证伪，应当作废。

(2) 但方向第一次与论文一致。本次 mmap-PF 两项在 ON 下更快(0.844/0.884)，正是论文 SS6.2 预期的
方向；而 mmap 两项在 ON 下略慢(1.085/1.068)，也正是论文预期的方向。两项同时与理论同号，这是此前
两轮都没出现的。(对照：跨启动 A/B 里 mmap-PF 是 1.029/1.065，方向与理论相反——说明那一轮是噪声。)
然而仍然不能下结论：四项 p 值最小只有 0.074，没有一项达到 0.05；组内离散 21%-50% 依旧远大于臂间
差异 6%-16%。「方向一致」可以是真实弱效应 + 大噪声，也可以是巧合。n=8 分不开。

结论(与 §10.70 同样的纪律)：x86_64 上的预标记性能依然无法判定。本轮把「能不能配对测量」这个
工程问题解决了(用 40 行代码替代了一次高风险启动协议改造)，但没有解决「能不能测出来」这个物理
问题。现在可以确定：这台共享宿主测不出来，无论用哪种设计。

要再进一步，只剩两条路，都不是「多跑几轮」：
1. 换测量环境：独占核(isolcpus + nohz_full + 绑核)甚至裸金属。当前噪声地板下任何统计都无法给出
   结论。
2. 换被测量：cortenmm_bench 的 mmap/mmap-pF 单次只有十几毫秒(1T=0.02s 量级)，样本本身就太短，
   一次调度抢占就能吞掉它。应当把每次迭代放大到数百毫秒以上(增大映射规模或迭代数)，让单次测量的
   时长超过噪声的相关时间——这比换宿主便宜得多，且当前就该先做。

在拿到组内离散降到个位数百分比的数据之前，不得声称「x86_64 上预标记性能中性」，也不得声称「已
复现论文的 mmap-PF 加速」。
20108bb514b1f061ee6d305239e33667f1f9f161:
test(bench): make benchmark rounds configurable and test a longer paired sample

§10.71 给了两条路，第二条是「换被测量」：当时 cortenmm_bench 每次测量只有 1T≈0.02s，一次
调度抢占就能吞掉整个样本。本轮把每次迭代放大到数百毫秒(ROUNDS 由编译期常量改为 argv[3] 可调，
同时修正 ops_out 用的是同一个值，避免 ops/s 被算错)，样本时长从 0.02s -> 0.21s(约 10 倍)，
单次启动内配对 A/B，10 轮。

结果(中位数, ns)：
  mmap    high  ON 52162  OFF 51545  1.012  离散 ON 64.2%/OFF 14.8%  p=0.257
  mmap    low   ON 53316  OFF 51550  1.034  离散 ON 59.0%/OFF 11.8%  p=0.070
  mmap-PF high  ON 138360 OFF 139192 0.994  离散 ON 32.7%/OFF 58.0%  p=0.326
  mmap-PF low   ON 138338 OFF 145650 0.950  离散 ON 35.1%/OFF 71.7%  p=0.290
日志自证 ON 臂生效：mm_anon_provisioned: 331536、mm_fault_from_status: 164676。

结论一：加长样本没有降低噪声地板(我的第二个假设也被自己的实验证伪)。离散度 32%-72%，比短样本
那轮(21%-50%)更差，mmap high 的 ON 离散高达 64%。至此两条降噪路线都失败了：
  跨启动交错(§10.70)            基线              20%-45%
  单次启动内配对(§10.71)        宿主漂移变共有噪声  21%-50%(没降)
  样本 x10 加长(§10.72)         样本超过噪声相关时间 32%-72%(更差)
结论应当写死：这台共享宿主测不出 <1.2x 的效应，与测量设计无关。主导噪声是宿主本身(其它租户抢占、
cache/THP 抖动、KVM 翻译缓冲)，它在每一次测量内部起作用，因此任何跨测量的统计设计都治不了它。

结论二：但短样本那一轮的大幅效应，基本是样本太短造成的假象。把三轮点估计并排看，比值随样本变长
系统性地向 1.0 收敛：
  mmap low          1.286 -> 1.034
  mmap-PF high  1.029(跨启动)/0.844(配对) -> 0.994
  mmap-PF low   1.065(跨启动)/0.884(配对) -> 0.950
  mmap high         1.017 -> 1.012
§10.70 那个「mmap 回归 29%」在样本长 10 倍后缩到 3.4%。这验证了当时「不把它当结论」是对的——
它确实只是噪声。同时，§10.71 里那个「两项同时与论文同号、可能是真实弱效应」的乐观读法也应当
收回：那些同号在大样本下并没有变强，而是一起塌回 1.0 附近。两组符号一致，原来更可能是巧合。

仍然不能下的结论：p 值最小 0.070，没有一项达到 0.05；离散 32%-72% 仍远大于臂间差异
0.6%-5%。所以依然不能说「x86_64 上预标记性能中性」。但可以说得比上一轮强一点：三轮一致指向
「效应若有，也在 5% 以内」，而 §10.70 那种量级的效应已被证明是测量假象。

下一步只有一个了：换测量环境(独占核 / 裸金属)。isolcpus + nohz_full 值得一试——它同时压低抢占
与 tick 干扰，是当前唯一还没试过的、能真正降低噪声地板的手段。在拿到组内离散降到个位数百分比的
数据之前，不得对 x86_64 性能下任何结论。
2acead9a98728e45b7fc4f5c90b79f7b538f0750:
docs(roadmap): record the shared-host limit on further x86_64 performance measurements

§10.72 指出唯一还没试过的降噪手段是 isolcpus + nohz_full。核对之后结论是在本机上不能做，也不该
做：
- isolcpus / nohz_full 是宿主内核启动参数，需要 root、需要重启宿主、并且会影响同一台机器上的
  所有其它租户。这不是「我的实验环境」，我没有权利为了自己的基准去改动它。
- 宿主侧的证据也支持「噪声来自外部」这一判断：load average: 4.72, 4.72, 5.51，2/1774 个可运行
  线程/总线程，16 核。即在我把 QEMU 绑到 12-15 的同时，别的租户仍在同一批核上活动——taskset
  只约束我的进程，约束不了别人。

所以 §10.72 那张表应当作为本机上的最终答案：
  跨启动交错          基线                20%-45%
  单次启动内配对      宿主漂移变共有噪声  21%-50%
  样本 x10 加长       样本超过噪声相关时间 32%-72%
  独占核 / nohz_full  真正压低噪声地板    不可用(需改共享宿主)

x86_64 上的预标记性能问题，在本机、在不改动宿主的前提下，已经无法解决。这不是「还没努力」，而是
环境上限。三轮实验的一致结论是：效应若有也在 5% 以内(长样本下 1.012/1.034/0.994/0.950)，而
§10.70 那种 1.29x 的大幅效应已被证明是短样本噪声。

要闭合这个问题，只能换机器：独占宿主或裸金属。在那之前，CortenMM 的性能结论只限 riscv64
(§10.34，TCG，配对 A/B，性能中性)，且必须注明 TCG 与 KVM 的绝对数值不可互相比较。
7132a1b915753a19ccd415252ffc1c92a212252f:
docs(roadmap): record the next step for faults without mm lock and the RSS race analysis

已核实当前状态：kernel/mm/fault.c 在 800 行取 spin_lock(&mm->lock)、1119 行才释放，而完全不查
VMA 的状态缺页路径(963-1010)就嵌在这个区间内部。因此论文最核心的那条主张——「缺页不碰 VMA
锁」——目前并未实现：状态路径确实不查 VMA，但它仍然在 mm 全局锁下运行，所有并发缺页(多核、
多线程)会在 mm->lock 上排队。这与 §10.33 测出的「性能中性」是一致的：拿不到 VMA 查找的收益，
因为那把锁的代价还在。

前置条件已经查清：卡点是 mm->rss 的数据竞争。
- mm->rss 是普通 size_t(vm.h:227)，不是原子量；
- fault.c 里有 12 处 rss++/rss +=，cow.c 另有 3 处；
- 状态路径自己也要 mm->rss++(fault.c:1010 附近)，而它必须在不持 mm->lock 的情况下做这件事；
- 更要紧的是读侧：cg_mem.c:125 在 OOM 选 victim 时读 t->mm->rss，而那段代码只持 proc_lock，不
  持 mm->lock：
      uint64_t pflags = spin_lock_irqsave(&proc_lock);
      ...
      size_t task_rss = t->mm ? t->mm->rss : 0;
      int score = (int)task_rss + t->policy.oom_score_adj;
  这已经是潜在的数据竞争(读者在 proc_lock 下，写者在 mm->lock 下，两者互不排斥)——现在能成立
  只是因为当前所有写者都恰好在 mm->lock 下、而 OOM 路径恰好不并发。一旦把状态路径移出
  mm->lock，这个竞争会立刻变成真 bug。

因此顺序是固定的，不能跳步：
1. 先把 mm->rss 变成原子/一致可读(__atomic_add_fetch 之类)，并让 OOM 的读侧用 acquire 语义读到
   一致值。这一步本身就是修一个既有隐患，即使不做状态路径改造也该做。
2. 再把状态路径的临界区从 mm->lock 移到页表游标锁之下。这一点设计上前途是通的：状态路径只碰
   per-PTE 元数据 + PT 项，而这些由 mm_addrspace_lock() 的 PT 页锁保护(pt.h:29-43 的注释正是这个
   契约)；它不需要 VMA 锁，因为它按设计不读 VMA 列表。真正要小心的是与 munmap/mremap 的页表拆表
   并发——mm_pt_read_enter() 的读侧令牌必须覆盖「判断 ANON_VIRT」到「写入 PT 项」全程，否则可能
   在别人拆表时把已拆掉的叶子重新写回去(这正是 §10.29 那类 PT 页 UAF 的形态)。
3. 第三步才是性能验证：这一步做完才有资格重新测 mmap-pf，而且必须在能降噪的环境上测
   (§10.73)，否则量出来的还是噪声。

明确不做的事：
- 不会为了「看起来无锁」而在状态路径里加 per-mm 序列号之类的伪无锁——§10.30 刚证明 per-metadata
  MCS 节点已经能把 cursor 往返成本降一个量级，说明瓶颈在锁的可扩展性而非锁的存在本身。
- 不会在共享宿主上用当前 bench 去证明收益(§10.72/§10.73 已证明测不出来)。

结论：这是当前最值得做的下一项工程，且第 1 步(rss 原子化)独立有价值、风险低、可以先做。但它是
多阶段改造，本轮上下文不足以安全完成第 2 步(页表游标锁的临界区重划 + 拆表并发的读侧令牌覆盖)并
做出可信验证，故按 §10.57 确立的纪律停在这里，不凭猜测下手。
2d6ed9c6557ac6d11ed1dc3fafd3a5a3e8f9e188:
docs(roadmap): correct the RSS atomicity risk assessment and identify required CAS sites

§10.74 写「第 1 步(rss 原子化)独立有价值、风险低、可以先做」。动手前先清点了站点，这个「风险低」
是低估了，据实更正。

全仓库 ->rss 共 52 处，跨 10 个文件。关键在于它们不是同一种形状：

(a) 简单加减——可用一次原子操作完成，风险低。fault.c 12 处(mm->rss++、t->mm->rss++、
    t->mm->rss += PMD_PAGE_COUNT、t->mm->rss += mapped)、elf.c 2、vm.c 1、cow.c 4、mremap.c 1。

(b) 读-改-写带夹取——这才是难点，简单原子操作是错的：
        mm->rss = (mm->rss > pages) ? mm->rss - pages : 0;   /* munmap.c:125,246 madvise.c:71,91 */
        mm->rss = mm->rss ? mm->rss - 1 : 0;                 /* oom.c:159 */
    这 5 处必须写成 CAS 循环才能既原子又不会下溢：
        size_t cur = __atomic_load_n(&mm->rss_atomic, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        for (;;) {
            size_t next = cur > pages ? cur - pages : 0;
            if (__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&mm->rss_atomic, &cur, next, 1,
                                            __ATOMIC_RELAXED, __ATOMIC_RELAXED))
                return;
        }
    若图省事改成 __atomic_sub_fetch 再夹取，会引入一个原先不存在的下溢窗口(读者已把值算小、另一
    线程又减了一次)。而 rss 直接喂给 OOM 选 victim(§10.74 的 cg_mem.c:125)，下溢会让 OOM 选出错误
    的牺牲者——这是一个安全性方向的真实回归，不是风格问题。

(c) 初始化/清零——vm.c:514,709、proc.c:605、exec.c:640(release store 即可)。

(d) 跨锁读取——fork.c:267(在 proc_lock 下打印)、cg_mem.c:125(OOM 选 victim，也在 proc_lock 下)。
    这两处必须用 acquire 语义读到一致值，否则只是把竞争从「非原子」换成「原子但撕裂」。

所以第 1 步的真实形状是：新增一组 helper(mm_rss_add / mm_rss_sub_clamped / mm_rss_set /
mm_rss_get) + 把字段改名以让编译器强制暴露全部 52 处 + 逐处按 (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) 分类改写 + 全架构
与全门验证。

这应当作为一次独立的、有人复核的改动单独做，而不是在一次性能会话的末尾顺手做掉。理由：它同时要
动 OOM 选人这条安全性路径，又需要覆盖 10 个文件的正确性验证；在没有余量去逐条复核的环境里做
这种改造，风险与收益不成比例。

但它依然值得做、且仍是第 1 步——因为它修的是一个已经存在的竞争隐患(写者在 mm->lock 下、OOM
读者在 proc_lock 下，两者互不排斥)，只是目前恰好因为「所有写者都持 mm->lock」而没有变成真 bug。
顺序依然不变：先 (d)+rss 原子化，再把状态路径移出 mm->lock，最后才谈性能。

ed2daedc563d8c5b53cbdffdd0bf7e8e5b55a09c:
feat(arch): enable SMEP/SMAP on x86_64 and PAN on AArch64 (feature-gated)

Every kernel access to user memory already goes through the direct-map copy
helpers in kernel/mm/mm.c, which check the PTE permission bits explicitly
first.  The kernel never dereferences a user virtual address directly, so
supervisor-mode access protection can be enabled without any stac/clac window
being needed around the copies.

- x86_64: trap_init() -- which runs on the BSP and on every AP -- gates
  CR4.SMEP and CR4.SMAP on CPUID leaf 7 EBX bit 7 (SMEP) and bit 20 (SMAP).
  QEMU's default qemu64 model does not advertise either bit, so the writes
  are a no-op there; -cpu host/max and real hardware take effect.
- aarch64: trap_init() gates SCTLR_EL1.PAN on the PAN field of
  ID_AA64MMFR1_EL1 ([23:20]).  cortex-a57 (v8.0) is a no-op, v8.1+ applies.

loongarch64 has no equivalent hardware mechanism, and ppc64le's KUAP is left
for later work.  riscv64's permissive SUM setting (a blanket SUM=1 in the
trap entry) is tightened separately.

Verified: smoke-x86_64 and smoke-aarch64 PASS on the default CPU models, i.e.
the no-op path; a full boot of both x86_64 and aarch64 with -cpu max reaches
mksh/telnetd with no fault, exercising the path where SMEP/SMAP/PAN are
actually live.
c89fabb9afc86b9c45d44aacb610ab48c9b23eb8:
feat(security): enforce user-space W^X, complete ASLR, and add a kernel stack canary

W^X: kernel/mm/wx.c adds mm_wx_filter_prot(), a single policy function that
mmap, mprotect and the ELF loader all pass through.  The default is deny, so
an RWX user mapping returns -EACCES; a boot can relax it with the cmdline key
a20.wx=strip|off.  A scan of all 195 static musl binaries in the tree found
zero PT_LOAD segments that need RWX, so nothing has to opt out today.

ASLR: kernel/mm/aslr.c reuses the core/random.c entropy pool.  The stack top
takes a page-aligned downward random offset (10 bits of entropy on 64-bit,
clamped by USER_STACK_FLOOR because of the fixed vdso layout); the mmap base
is randomised per process (20 bits on 64-bit), replacing the hardcoded
MMAP_BASE_ADDR; the brk start takes a random offset.  fork inherits the
layout rather than re-randomising it, which is what Linux does.

Stack protection: kernel/core/stack_protector.c provides __stack_chk_guard
(randomised once the entropy pool is ready) and __stack_chk_fail.  The kernel
CFLAGS default to -fstack-protector-strong, which CONFIG_STACK_PROTECTOR can
turn off.

Verified: riscv64, x86_64 and aarch64 kernels build with zero warnings;
smoke-riscv64 and smoke-abi-linux PASS.  The new
user/cmds/stress/wx_aslr_test.c checks that RWX is refused and that the stack
and mmap addresses differ across two execs.

Remaining: entropy quality is limited early in the riscv64 and aarch64 boots,
and the stack is limited to 10 bits because of the existing fixed layout --
widening it means rearranging the user address space.

smoke-iommu-udriver-isolation now asserts the counters.  End to end with the

done.

a00e7e0c2c95273f7daebd077caaf787ad790a38:
feat(coredump): generate an ELF core dump on fatal signals

kernel/proc/coredump.c is an ELF64 ET_CORE generator: one PT_NOTE holding
NT_PRSTATUS, NT_FPREGSET and NT_PRPSINFO, plus one PT_LOAD per VMA.  Register
export reuses ptrace's arch_ptrace_export_regs(), and the file is written
through the VFS write path.

It is hooked into both fatal paths: the fatal default-action branch of
signal_deliver_user(), and the unhandled-hardware-fault fast path in trap.c's
deliver_user_sync_signal().  The latter also fixes the wait status to carry the
0x80 WCOREDUMP bit, matching Linux.

RLIMIT_CORE is now wired up end to end: stored in signal_state, inherited
across fork, preserved across exec, and honoured by getrlimit, setrlimit and
prlimit64.  A limit of 0 produces nothing.

The core_pattern procfs stub is connected to real reads and writes and
supports the placeholder subset %p %e %s %u %g %t; |pipe is unsupported and
that boundary is recorded.

Added user/cmds/stress/coredump_test.c and a smoke-coredump gate.

Verified: smoke-coredump PASS (SIGSEGV produces an ET_CORE with all three
notes, and the RLIMIT_CORE=0 negative case produces no file); the resulting
core was cross-checked with the host's file and readelf.

Boundaries: 64-bit only, NT_FILE is not emitted, non-resident pages are
written as zero, and the VMA snapshot is capped at 1024.
386d9283f34c968f3ed7b5e5da8835d4137bdf1b:
fix(mm): retain VMO frames until process-exit teardown completes

The root cause was in free_vma_pages() (kernel/mm/vma.c): on the process-exit
mm teardown path it called frame_put() on PTEs belonging to VM_VMO mappings,
violating the VMO ownership contract.  A VMO owns its frames; unmapping a PTE
never releases them.  Both mm_munmap_locked and the madvise path already
skipped VM_VMO correctly -- only the exit path did not.

The consequences match the historical symptoms.  When a shmring child exits,
the shared VMO's frames are returned to the buddy allocator while the VMO is
still alive, the parent is still mapping them and vmo->pages[] still points at
them.  Those frames get reused as kernel stacks, anonymous pages and page
tables, and the ring data path keeps writing through the stale mapping,
overwriting arbitrary kernel structures -- this is where the idle-spinning
kernel stack pages, the corrupted pfa free list and Alpine's "corrupted kernel
stack pointer" all came from.  A later vmo_destroy returned them a second time
(double free plus stale buddy metadata), which is what the shutdown audit saw
as a count mismatch and orphan sub-chains.

The fix, in three parts:
- vma.c: free_vma_pages() skips VM_PFNMAP|VM_VMO, consistent with munmap.
- cow.c: mm_fork_clone_leaf() no longer frame_get()s a VM_VMO mapping.  The
  VMA already holds a vmo_ref, so taking a frame reference would now leak.
- mremap.c: neither move path frame_get()s or frame_put()s a VM_VMO frame.

kernel/mm/frame.c gains permanent forensics hardening: an orphan-frame scan
over the freemap, a membership trap in fl_remove, buddy merging that requires
freemap membership at the chain position, fl_push_clean to prevent double
listing, an immediate panic in frame_get when rc==0, and frame_trace extended
to cover pfa_free.

Verified in an isolated worktree (baseline plus this fix only):
smoke-native-shmring passed 10 consecutive runs, each followed by a clean
poweroff and a shutdown audit with errors=0; smoke-riscv64 and smoke-proc-stress
PASS.  Before the fix this scenario reproduced
[PFA CORRUPT] remove of non-head head-claimant 100% of the time.
c3c70fc09027ad09dbaa1779a10fbe1c0d997a47:
fix(riscv64): drop blanket SUM=1 from the user trap entry and close the doc entry

The user trap entry in `kernel/arch/riscv64/trap/trap.S` set `sstatus` with
`(1 << 8) | (1 << 18)`, so `SPP=1` and `SUM=1` together. That blanket `SUM=1` is
backwards with respect to the intent of SMAP-style protection: the kernel reaches
user memory only through the direct-map copy helpers in `kernel/mm/mm.c`, which
do an explicit PTE permission check first, and it never dereferences a user
virtual address directly. The trap path therefore has no use for `SUM`, and the
constant is now just `li t0, (1 << 8)`.

With `SUM` kept at 0, any supervisor-mode access to a user page that slipped
through faults immediately, which together with the `frame.c` and trap forensics
turns into a panic that preserves the crime scene. That is the same shape of
defence as x86_64 SMAP and aarch64 PAN.

Verified: `smoke-riscv64` and `smoke-abi-linux` PASS. That path covers the full
musl exec/syscall/signal/copy chain, so any hidden direct dereference would
surface there. The claim is scoped to those two smoke gates, which is what
establishes the absence of a hidden direct user dereference along that chain.

`docs/security/hardening.md` is updated to match. The riscv64 SUM blanket section
moves from "in progress" to closed, and now records that the blanket `SUM=1` is
removed with `SUM` kept at 0, that any missed supervisor-mode access to a user
page faults immediately and, combined with the `frame.c` forensics hardening,
becomes a panic with the scene preserved, and that `smoke-riscv64` and
`smoke-abi-linux` found no hidden direct dereference.
93f18a697277a603b99f1b30326607723e59163e:
feat(elf): back-fill the eager head page only when no earlier PT_LOAD mapped it

Root cause of a ufsd SIGSEGV that has been present since 3d986c53.  For a
static ET_EXEC with an independent BSS PT_LOAD whose filesz is 0, the linker
emits a placeholder p_offset that merely satisfies page congruence.  The BSS
first page is shared with the tail of .data, and map_segment's eager fallback
back-filled the file content preceding p_offset -- the ELF header and program
headers -- into that live page unconditionally, overwriting the .data that had
just been mapped.  g_ext4_vnode_ops.lookup ended up holding a phdr scalar
(0xc28), so the first ext4 directory lookup jumped away.

The back-fill now happens only when the page was not already mapped by an
earlier PT_LOAD.  The AT_PHDR case, where the first LOAD back-fills the ELF
header, behaves exactly as before.

Verified in a clean worktree: smoke-native-fs-all PASS (it crashed
unconditionally before), and smoke-native-svc, smoke-native-registry and
smoke-riscv64 PASS.
412ece10de1a1fff37cbe24de8d22df5414f0be4:
fix(coredump): include UINT64_MAX in NOMMU builds

The NOMMU build does not pick up stdint.h transitively through the MMU
headers, so the include is now explicit.

Verified: ARCH=riscv64 NOMMU=1 kernel-only builds.
7d59c0242718f3c3465ee0c93693a26dc067b39f:
refactor(kernel): split kernel-image segments for W^X (KXAN) and tag drvmod modules

On riscv64, x86_64 and aarch64 the boot huge page is the final kernel mapping,
so it is rebuilt in place.  The RAM huge page is downgraded to a shared
intermediate-level table of 2 MiB NX blocks, the kernel image is split per
segment at 4 KiB granularity (text ROX, rodata RO, data and bss RW+NX), the
direct map is made NX, and aarch64 gets SCTLR_EL1.WXN back.  The new tables are
built completely and only then written in to replace the active entries, so
there is no window in which mappings are invalid.

finalize ends with a four-point permission self-check that panics on failure
and prints a [KXAN] line on success.  The drvmod module layout changed to put
text and data on separate pages; after loading, arch_kwx_module_protect() makes
the text region RX.

This also fixes a pre-existing x86_64 boot crash that HEAD carried: once the
stack canary was in, the x86_64 compiler emitted a TLS-style canary at
%fs:0x28, and with a kernel-mode FS base of 0 that faulted before anything
else.  trap_init now installs a kernel FS stub per CPU and trap.S switches to it
on entry.

Verified: smoke-riscv64, smoke-abi-linux, smoke-x86_64, smoke-aarch64 and
smoke-smp-bringup (2 CPUs) all PASS; the visionfive2 and virtualbox-aarch64
boards compile.

Boundaries, documented in docs/security/kernel-wx.md: loongarch64 goes through
a DMW direct-translation window with no segment granularity, so it is out of
reach; ppc64le, arm32 and riscv32 are untouched behind weak empty
implementations; and aarch64 has no remote TLB shootdown, so module tagging
only issues a local tlbi.
24c963bae75e4af9a35dd7a18f1f421a9c58301f:
feat(ns): mount namespaces, and an unshare/setns that says no honestly

- New mnt_namespace_t in kernel/fs/vfs/mntns.c: a private mount table with a
  refcount and an ino registry, hung off task_t.mnt_ns where NULL means the
  initial namespace.
- fork and clone share the reference, CLONE_NEWNS and unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)
  deep-copy the table, and exit releases it idempotently through a
  fdtable_close_all hook.  The process core was off-limits for this change, so
  that hook is the compromise and it is explained in a comment there.
- Every public API in vfs/mount.c now operates implicitly on the calling task's
  namespace, so no call site changed.  Path resolution, mount, umount,
  fscontext, /proc and /proc/mounts are isolated per caller automatically.
- Deep-copied entries are marked VFS_MOUNT_NS_SHARED, so a umount in a child
  namespace only detaches that table entry instead of destroying a filesystem
  the other namespace still uses.
- /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt carries a real ino and pins its target, so setns still
  works after that process exits.  The other ns types render a static singleton
  ino and are refused honestly: unshare and setns return -EINVAL instead of
  faking success, and clone/clone3 whitelist CLONE_NEWNS and really create it.
- user/cmds/stress/mntns_test.c adds 12 assertion groups plus a smoke-mntns
  gate.

Verified: smoke-mntns, smoke-vfs-edge, smoke-vfs-stress, smoke-abi-linux and
smoke-riscv64 all PASS.

Semantic boundaries: no mount propagation; /proc/<pid>/mounts reflects the
reader's namespace; and the permission model is CAP_SYS_ADMIN or same uid,
since there is no userns yet.
1ccf5b1e4777d0bb7a2baceae119b38d3433e548:
refactor(abi): promote the poll and timer areas to full

poll:
- epoll_pwait2 rounds a sub-millisecond timeout up.  It used to truncate to
  zero and return immediately.
- select, pselect6 and ppoll validate negative tv_sec/tv_nsec with EINVAL,
  and ppoll additionally requires sigsetsize == 8.
- The new tests lock down behaviour that was already correct: ET and LT,
  EPOLLONESHOT, POLLNVAL/HUP/ERR, a dup sharing the interest list, nested
  epoll ELOOP refusal, and eventfd semantics.

timer:
- kernel/proc/timer_posix.c is rewritten.  timer_gettime returns the remaining
  time, it_value == 0 disarms, TIMER_ABSTIME is converted per clockid, periodic
  timers rearm without drift, overrun counting is real, SIGEV_THREAD and
  illegal notify/signo combinations are refused, and the CPU-time clockids
  return EOPNOTSUPP explicitly.
- ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF now actually deliver their signals, driven
  from a scheduler tick accounting point.
- clock_nanosleep is rewritten: EINTR with the remaining time, an ABSTIME in
  the past returns immediately, and the arguments are validated -- including
  the negative tv_sec that used to wrap around into an eternal sleep.
- timerfd: TFD_TIMER_ABSTIME conversion fixed, flags validated, and
  TFD_TIMER_CANCEL_ON_SET implemented with a realtime-set generation counter.
- kernel/proc/timer_heap.c extracts an IRQ-safe signal-timer scan called from
  both the IRQ side and sched(), which fixes POSIX timers and SIGALRM never
  firing while the system was idle.

It also fixes a pre-existing regression: sys_fanotify_mark called strlen
directly on a user pointer and hung once SUM had been tightened, so it now goes
through user_path_strncpy.  syscall_ext.c's ALSA test is aligned with the real
asound.h ABI from cab83260.

New gates smoke-poll-edge (12 groups) and smoke-timer-edge (12 groups).  The
coverage table moves the poll and timer areas from partial to full; the
nanosleep restart limitation is the one exception and is noted as such.

Verified: both new gates plus smoke-riscv64, smoke-abi-linux, smoke-proc-stress
and smoke-syscall-ext all PASS, and check-doc-drift PASS.
8d1c3ac29660187425f8a60c7ef4a534c17fb8b0:
docs(net): assess the next horizon -- netfilter, dynamic libc, ext4 journal, power

Records where four large directions stand today, what each would cost, and
where to start.  None of them is implemented in this round; this is the
factual basis and the path for a later one.
6e2758c88ec08e6c67a36f6222fc505b7f5e5674:
feat(net): implement SIOCGIFCONF so user space can enumerate interfaces

net_vfile_ioctl() listed A20_SIOCGIFCONF in the dispatch that feeds
net_vfile_ifreq_ioctl(), but that switch had no case for it, so the request
fell through to -ENOTTY.  getifaddrs(), ifconfig and busybox `ip` are all
built on SIOCGIFCONF, and the per-interface getters that the same switch does
implement (SIOCGIFADDR, SIOCGIFNETMASK, SIOCGIFHWADDR, SIOCGIFFLAGS,
SIOCGIFINDEX) are unreachable without a way to discover which interfaces to
ask about.  A data plane that works but cannot list its interfaces is
invisible to ordinary user space.

Both Linux call shapes are handled: a NULL ifc_buf is the size query and
returns the exact byte count of a full listing, which is what callers size
their second pass from.  The family filter follows Linux in reading the wanted
family from the first entry of a non-empty buffer; since only IPv4 is
reported, a caller asking for another family gets an empty list rather than
IPv4 rows tagged with the wrong family.

The name is copied by length rather than as a C string because this tree's
lwIP pins `char name[2]`, a fixed non-terminated field.  A _Static_assert
pins the struct ifreq wire layout to 32 bytes, since user space walks the
buffer in whole-entry strides.

Verified: builds clean under -Werror -Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=undefined and
the kernel links (riscv64 linux-abi dev build).  Not yet exercised in a guest
-- there is no runtime gate for the SIOCGIF* area, so this needs one before
the behaviour can be called verified.

SIOCSIFMTU / SIOCSIFDSTADDR / SIOCSIFBRDADDR remain dispatched-but-unimplemented
and still return -ENOTTY rather than a faked success.
577d0cbd28dee3dd387a45f13a8481ca50049a2d:
fix(mm): compare mmap failure errno correctly on 32-bit architectures

At the end of proc_mmap(), "mmap failed" was decided with
`(int64_t)ret < 0 && (int64_t)ret >= -4095`, but ret is a pointer-width
integer.  Converting a pointer to a signed type wider than itself zero-extends
it, so on 32-bit targets (int64_t)ret is always in 0..0xFFFFFFFF: the first
half of the test is always true and the second always false, which made the
whole mmap-failure diagnostic path dead code.  On arm32, riscv32, loongarch32
and armv7m not a single failed mmap left a log line.

The test now goes through (long), which has the same width as a pointer, so a
negative value keeps its sign and the errno range (-4095, 0] is the same
expression on both 32- and 64-bit.
b33e2479855b59a09642981b0e0e6c8d2aa426ba:
build(swap): disable CONFIG_SWAP on architectures without swap PTE encoding

CONFIG_SWAP now defaults to y, but riscv32 and loongarch32 never defined a
swap PTE encoding (pte_is_swap / pte_to_swp_entry / swp_entry_to_pte in
kernel/arch/<arch>/include/page_table.h).  On those two, CONFIG_SWAP=y is not
merely an empty feature: kernel/mm/{fault,mm,munmap}.c and kernel/proc/exit.c
fail to compile outright.

This follows the shape the NOMMU gate already uses -- turn the feature off at
the point ARCH is chosen, rather than letting the build blow up halfway
through.  The comment states what is missing and where it breaks, so nobody
later mistakes the gate for a redundant special case and deletes it.
77ca3143ded0fe60578aeb46ccf26d9e0c73be6d:
docs(hybrid-kernel): sync the registered syscall counts (Linux 366 / Native 142)

The poll/timer edge work, mount namespaces, coredump and the rest each added
syscall entries as they landed, but the counts quoted in the narrative docs
had been sitting at 361 / 141.  The registered count is the one quick signal a
reader has for the size of the interface tables, so the drift actively
misleading anyone reasoning about "how much of Linux does Native ABI cover".

The numbers were checked against the LINUX_SYSCALL / NATIVE_SYSCALL entries in
kernel/abi/{linux,native}/syscall_table.def (366 / 142) rather than estimated.
78dd472e946810c1e7e22cbbb705c7bb24eabf8d:
docs(roadmap): record keep only unfinished items in the roadmap, move the rest to fact docs

a20os-improvement-todo.md had become a milestone checkbox ledger: most of its
255 lines were completed [x] entries, each carrying its own evidence trail, the
mistakes made along the way and a dated PASS.  The problem is that one document
was doing two mutually exclusive jobs --

  1. a to-do list, answering "what should I work on now"
  2. a change log, answering "what was done before, and how"

Job 2 is already done better by source comments, the commit history and the
fact documents, and the three drift apart over time.  The result was records
like "PASS on 2026-08" or "reproduced against 720e16ab0" that only mean
something at one point in time, so a reader cannot tell which still hold -- and
genuinely unfinished work drowned in finished entries.  The shmring/pfa entry
alone ran to twenty-odd lines across a dozen revisions, whose compressed content
amounts to the last sentence: the root cause was free_vma_pages calling
frame_put on a VM_VMO.

Changes:
- The roadmap now records only unfinished items; an entry is deleted as it
  lands, and no completed checkbox is kept.  Evidence for finished work is
  looked up in the fact documents and the commit history.
- docs/testing-gates.md gains the four gate entries that were missing (poll and
  timer edge semantics, mount namespace, fatal-signal core dump, swap), each
  with How to run / What it checks / When it fails.  This is where "move the
  finished items into the fact documents" actually lands.
- docs/security/hardening.md folds the riscv64 SUM blanket and the kernel-image
  W^X segment split into the feature table at the top: they are closed
  capabilities, not standalone risk sections, and keeping a closed "in progress"
  subsection around is more misleading than not writing one.
- The namespaces row of syscall_coverage.md now records the real mount
  namespace object model (mnt_ns, the CLONE_NEWNS deep copy, joining through
  /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt), and keeps the boundaries -- no mount propagation, no
  userns, permission model is CAP_SYS_ADMIN or same uid -- so having an object
  model does not promote it to full.
217a9b286bc23265b9f03736af55d19cdd08eaf3:
feat(net): expose the user-space network control surface

Completes the SIOCGIFCONF work started in 5c64d839 and adds the runtime gate
that area never had.  Writing that gate first is what surfaced the three real
defects below; two of them are older than this series.

SIOCGIFCONF now works end to end, but only after fixing what it depends on:

- `struct a20_ifreq` was 32 bytes.  musl/glibc's is 40 on LP64 (32 on ILP32),
  because the union is sized by `struct ifmap` (8+8+2+3, padded to 24).  The
  kernel emitted 3 whole entries in 96 bytes and user space, walking the buffer
  in 40-byte strides, saw them straddled.  A self-consistent private pair of
  structs would have hidden this, which is why netctl.c deliberately asserts
  against musl's own <net/if.h> definitions.  The struct now includes an
  ifmap so the size tracks `unsigned long` the way upstream's does, and both
  widths are asserted instead of one hardcoded constant.

- The loopback netif had no name at all.  g_loopif is a zero-initialised
  static and a20_lwip_loopif_init_cb never set one, so netif_find("lo*"),
  SIOCGIFADDR("lo*") and netif_name_to_index on loopback all failed.  Pre-
  existing, and unrelated to SIOCGIFCONF; it only became visible once
  something started listing interfaces.

- A netif's identity here is (name[0], name[1], num), and the vendored
  netif_find parses the number out of name[2] and rejects a name with no digit
  there.  So the two-byte lwIP name is not a name user space can resolve, and
  the composed "%c%c%u" spelling -- the one /proc/net/status already used --
  is the only correct thing to report or accept.

/proc/net/dev and /proc/net/route rendered a bare header and nothing else,
which is why "is net0 even up" had to be answered by guesswork in the guest.
They now project real state.  /proc/net/dev needed real counters to exist
first, so the RX drain and linkoutput now maintain per-netif byte/packet/
error/drop counts in the netif state, incremented at the two data-plane points
that already run under g_lwip_lock.  /proc/net/route reports each netif's
default gateway, which is the only route this stack holds -- it has no FIB,
and inventing rows for one would be worse than reporting one honest route.
Loopback bypasses the driver path, so its counters read zero, which is the
true value rather than a missing statistic.

MSG_OOB is now refused with EOPNOTSUPP at both funnels instead of being
silently ignored, which had been handing back ordinary in-band bytes as if
they were the urgent one.  MSG_NOSIGNAL deliberately needs no change: the
kernel only ever raises SIGPIPE from kernel/fs/pipe.c, never on a socket, so a
dead-peer write already reports EPIPE whether or not the flag is passed.

The gate is smoke-netctl (netctl.c, riscv64, static musl).  It sets
NET_HOSTFWD= because it only inspects local state and must not need host port
5555 free, which also stops it colliding with a concurrent run.

Verified on this commit: smoke-netctl PASS (3 interfaces enumerated, 0 panics),
smoke-network-suite PASS, smoke-poll-edge PASS, check-doc-drift PASS.  The
riscv64 dev build is clean under -Werror -Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=undefined.

Still absent by design, and reported as -ENOTTY rather than faked:
SIOCSIFMTU (needs NET_IOCTL_GET_MTU plumbed to the driver class; the static
1536-byte frame buffers cap MTU at 1500 regardless), SIOCSIFDSTADDR and
SIOCSIFBRDADDR.  There is still no routing netlink, so `ip` and NetworkManager
remain unusable, and /proc/net/arp is still a bare header because lwIP exposes
no ARP-table accessor.
92c84b6b388750407ed5be99cb0569de3c6cf290:
feat(net): add NETLINK_ROUTE so ip link and ip addr can enumerate interfaces

AF_NETLINK previously accepted only SOCK_DIAG, KOBJECT_UEVENT and GENERIC, so
`ip` failed at socket(AF_NETLINK) with EPROTONOSUPPORT and NetworkManager had
no way to discover interfaces.  RTM_GETLINK, RTM_GETADDR and RTM_GETROUTE now
dump real netif state, each dump terminated by NLMSG_DONE as iproute2 expects.

Netif state is snapshotted under g_lwip_lock and the lock dropped before any
reply is enqueued, because docs/net/network-lock-contract.md forbids holding
g_lwip_lock together with g_net_lock.

Three bugs surfaced only by running the new gate, all of them mine:

- net_enqueue_msg_locked() returns the byte count, so testing it against 0
  skipped the NLMSG_DONE terminator entirely.  A dump reader then waits for a
  second datagram that never arrives, and the test hung instead of failing.
- musl's send() passes a pointer to a zeroed sockaddr with addrlen 0, so an
  absent address arrives looking like a present AF_UNSPEC one.  Validating on
  `if (addr)` alone rejected every ordinary send().
- The payload is assembled after the header offset, because the header is
  written last and would otherwise overwrite the leading ifinfomsg.  With the
  payload built at offset 0 the attributes were intact but ifinfomsg was
  clobbered, so every link arrived with no IFLA_IFNAME and `ip link` would have
  had no name to display.

Also adds the netlink half of smoke-netctl: the wire structs are restated in
the test rather than included, because this tree's musl ships no
<linux/netlink.h>, and an independently restated contract is what makes it a
test of the kernel rather than a mirror of it.  It asserts the dumps end with
NLMSG_DONE, that every link carries IFLA_IFNAME, and that a link exists
implies an address object -- SIOCGIFCONF and RTM_GETADDR must not disagree
about whether an interface has IPv4.

Unrelated to the netlink work: kernel/include/proc/signal.h was missing the
prototype for signal_fatal_exit_code_dumped(), which signal.c defines and
trap.c calls, so the tree did not build.  Added the one-line declaration
alongside its two siblings.  Drop this hunk if that coredump work is being
restructured.

Verified on this commit: smoke-netctl PASS (3 interfaces, netlink dumps
included, 0 panics), smoke-network-suite PASS, smoke-poll-edge PASS,
check-doc-drift PASS.  Note that smoke-network-suite and smoke-poll-edge need
host port 5555 free and will fail with a bare QEMU hostfwd error when another
run holds it; smoke-netctl sets NET_HOSTFWD= and is immune.

Boundaries, reported rather than faked: there is no FIB, so RTM_GETROUTE
reports only each netif's default gateway and RTM_SET* plus route mutation
return EOPNOTSUPP.  /proc/net/arp is still a bare header because lwIP exposes
no ARP-table accessor.  SIOCSIFMTU/SIOCSIFDSTADDR/SIOCSIFBRDADDR remain
dispatched-but-unimplemented and still return ENOTTY.

TLS needed no change after all: building the real xfce rootfs shows libssl.so.3,
libcrypto.so.3, libcurl.so.4, libgnutls, libmbedtls and the ca-certificates
bundle are already present, pulled in transitively by apk's resolver.  The
absence was only visible in packages/world/xfce.world, which lists directly
named packages.
09afa21634ff9e9c369788b63437796f89490241:
fix(audit): close the defects the 2026-09 hardening round left open

A claim-by-claim audit of the seventeen commits in ae36b271..HEAD found
several places where the delivered code did not match what the commit
messages and docs asserted.  Each fix below is tied to a specific claim
that was otherwise false or unfinished.

Mount namespaces -- mntns_copy_mounts() marked the *source* entry
VFS_MOUNT_NS_SHARED, and vfs_umount() then skipped the filesystem
destructor for it.  The moment any process called unshare(CLONE_NEWNS),
every mount in the init namespace became permanently un-teardownable, so
umount() returned success while leaking the superblock, the uxfs channel
and the block-device binding forever.  mount_t gains ns_users, the count
of namespaces holding the entry; a copy only ever detaches, and the
destructor runs for the source once nothing else holds it.  mntns_test
gained a thirteenth group that mounts before the unshare and checks the
owning namespace still has the mount after another namespace detaches it
-- the shared path the previous twelve groups never touched.

listns(2) returned nsid 0 for every nstype, contradicting the
/proc/<pid>/ns/mnt id the same process would read.  It now reports the
real mount-namespace id, the Linux init inos for the singleton types, and
-EINVAL for anything A20OS has no namespace for.  mntns_init_ns() was
exported but had no caller and is gone; the init-ns inos now come from
mntns.h instead of being spelled out twice.

coredump: the 0x80 WCOREDUMP bit was set for every core-dump-by-default
signal whether or not a file was written, so RLIMIT_CORE=0 still told
coredump(3) and gdb a core existed.  coredump_on_fatal_signal() now
returns whether it wrote one and the bit follows that; the four fatal
paths that cannot dump pass 0.  A limit-clamped segment also left
p_offset unaligned against p_vaddr, which readelf rejects -- it now
rounds down to a page multiple.

mremap of a VM_VMO VMA copied the flag but not the vmo pointer, so the
destination mapped frames the source teardown then freed.  Both the move
and the duplicate path now inherit vmo/vmo_offset and take the reference.

Native-ABI net_bind/net_connect/net_accept/net_getname handed raw user
pointers to the core, which dereferenced them in supervisor mode -- the
one thing the riscv64 SUM, x86_64 SMAP and aarch64 PAN changes assume
never happens.  They now stage through kernel buffers like the Linux ABI
already did.  riscv64 also clears the SUM bit explicitly rather than
relying on nothing ever setting it.

loop devices could be rebound while a swap area was live, after which
swap wrote its own offsets into the new backing file.  A claimed flag
refuses LOOP_SET_FD/LOOP_CLR_FD until the last consumer releases it, and
/proc/swaps now reads through swap_list_area() under the per-area lock
instead of touching a name that swap_unregister_device() frees.

Also: sethostname/setdomainname wrote buf[len] with an unbounded len past
a 65-byte stack frame; the /dev/loopN index parser overflowed a signed
int; the IOMMU fault path disabled the device context but left PCI bus
mastering on until the driver's next poll, and its QEMU<=10.0 PPN
exception is now behind CONFIG_IOMMU_TRRESP_LEGACY_PPN instead of
unconditional.

Verified: kernel-only builds clean for riscv64, loongarch64, aarch64,
x86_64, ppc64le and riscv64 NOMMU; riscv32 builds again once CONFIG_SWAP
is forced off where there is no swap PTE encoding.  smoke-mntns (with
the new group), smoke-coredump, smoke-swap, smoke-poll-edge,
smoke-timer-edge and smoke-abi-linux PASS; check-doc-drift PASS.

smoke-native-shmring still hangs at pid 6.  It is recorded in the roadmap
as a pre-existing defect: the 2026-08 pfa free-list entry already notes
the gate reproducing on the baseline, and a per-commit scan shows no
commit in this range introduces it.
22a3f31ed1a8183137dd27ceb437e3c576ac7d88:
feat(qemu): expose the GPU device option and honor extra_qemu at runtime

The 3D (virgl) path could not be reached from any shipped configuration:
every GUI instance used the 2D-only virtio-gpu variant, so the host never
offered VIRTIO_GPU_F_VIRGL and every 3D ioctl failed with -ENXIO.  The
capability was present but unreachable.

- Extract the GPU device out of the per-arch GUI device strings into
  QEMU_GPU_<arch>, matching the existing QEMU_BLK_<arch>/QEMU_NET_<arch>
  pattern, and select the -gl- variant when GPU_3D=1.  2D stays the
  default, so no existing invocation changes.
- Note that virglrenderer runs host-side: a TCG guest still gets host-GPU
  rendering, which is the only way to exercise 3D on the arches that have
  no KVM.

machine.extra_qemu was also dead on the run/debug path -- only
tools/a20_test.py appended it -- so a manifest could not add a device to
`tools/a20 run` even though docs/instances.md documents the field.

- Derive it as EXTRA_QEMU and append it in the Makefile, making the
  Makefile the single source of truth for the QEMU command line.
- Drop the now-duplicate append in a20_test.py (verified: the IOMMU smoke
  still gets exactly one riscv-iommu-pci).
a289b7bcbe5021448630a52190f8d877158acd24:
feat(drm): model buffers as GEM objects

GBM cannot create a rendering buffer on A20OS: there is no GEM object
model at all, only the legacy dumb-buffer path.  Introduce GEM the way
Linux models it, since GBM and the virtgpu 3D path are both written
against that ABI.

- Rename drm_buffer_t to drm_gem_t and grow the store from 16 to 64
  entries.  A GEM object is a VMO plus metadata; a dumb buffer is a GEM
  object that also carries a linear layout, so there is now one buffer
  abstraction rather than two parallel ones.
- Add GEM_CREATE, GEM_MMAP, GEM_OPEN and GEM_GET_HANDLE, plus the
  name->handle table that backs cross-process transfer.
- GEM_MMAP returns the same `handle << PAGE_SHIFT` encoding MAP_DUMB
  already used, so the existing mmap path serves both without change.
- Make GEM_CLOSE actually release the object.  It was a deliberate no-op
  that leaked every GEM handle, which is fine for a compositor's handful
  of dumb buffers and not fine for a renderer allocating thousands.
- Funnel dumb-buffer creation through the shared allocator instead of
  duplicating slot-finding and handle assignment, and move handle
  allocation to a device-global counter (the per-open counter could mint
  duplicate handles against the global store).
- Add MODE_GETFB2, which libdrm issues while probing and which was an
  EINVAL hole.

The DRM_CAP_* ids in the header are libdrm's *legacy* GET_CAP numbering,
which is not the same order as the newer DRM_CAP_* in the kernel's
include/uapi/drm/drm.h.  Verified against the libdrm header rather than
from memory, because getting it wrong silently disables PRIME and dumb
discovery for every client.

Gates: smoke-riscv64 PASS, smoke-abi-linux PASS, check-instances OK.
b544121d3859690443eaee5b30c7ac47195e4d82:
docs(graphics): correct the 3D status and target UAPI

The 3D documentation asserted a capability that no gate could confirm.
Worse, the planned remedy ("implement DRM_IOCTL_VIRGL_*") was aimed at
the wrong ABI, so following it would have produced a lot of correct code
that Mesa still could not use.

Correcting the record:

- 3d-graphics.md's banner claimed "the kernel-side 3D command path is
  usable" and offered `GPU3D_TEST: PASS` as proof.  Neither held: the
  test never called SUBMIT_3D (it allocated an empty texture and tore it
  down), and it returned 0 on 2D-only devices, so it was green in every
  configuration and carried no information.  Replace the banner with a
  per-capability status table pointing at the gap for each item.
- xfce-wayland-adaptation.md was marked "historical" in one line and then
  read as current work throughout.  It describes user/wayland/,
  wayland-session.c, run-gui-* and smoke-qemu-gui-*, all deleted in
  8faae7a9.  State that plainly, and note that the compositor is now
  upstream labwc, not an OS-owned implementation.

The correction that matters most: modern Mesa's virtio_gpu_dri.so speaks
DRM_IOCTL_VIRTGPU_* (virtgpu_drm.h, nr 0x41-0x4b), not the legacy

94ba503d97c4a13bfe147ba323623d4b11e36123:
feat(virtgpu): implement the VIRTGPU UAPI, with 3D resources that have backing

This is the piece that decides whether stock Mesa can attach at all.
A20OS had only the private A20_GPU_IOCTL_* fork, which no upstream driver
speaks, so virtio_gpu_dri.so could never load -- regardless of how well
the transport worked.

Numbers come from the kernel's own uapi/drm/virtgpu_drm.h, not from the
legacy 'A'-family DRM_IOCTL_VIRGL_* that modern Mesa abandoned.  Every
one was re-derived against the _IOWR encoding and checked against the
header before use, and none collide with the existing DRM_IOCTL_* range.

Kernel side:

- GETPARAM, GET_CAPS, RESOURCE_CREATE, RESOURCE_INFO, EXECBUFFER, WAIT,
  MAP, CONTEXT_INIT and both TRANSFER directions.
- 3D resources are carried by a GEM handle, as in Linux, and the kernel
  publishes that object's pages with RESOURCE_ATTACH_BACKING.  This was
  the real gap: a 3D resource previously had no host-side memory, so an
  accepted command stream would still have operated on nothing.  Pages
  are materialised with vmo_get_page_charged rather than vmo_peek_page,
  because the host writes results into them and an unallocated page has
  no frame to write to.
- virtgl contexts are per-open and created lazily, matching Linux's
  virtgpu_fprivs.  GET_CAPSET also needs a live context: with ctx_id 0 the
  host answers ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which cost one debugging round.
- Backing arrays are kernel-built physical addresses, so they cannot go
  through ioctl()'s copy_from_user path.  Added purpose-built ops to
  gpu_dev_ops_t instead, keeping virtio-gpu details in virtio_gpu.c and
  GEM semantics in drm.c.

Verified in the guest, and the gate still fails when it should:

  GPU_3D=1 -> GETPARAM 3D_FEATURES=1, capset mask=0x7,
              GEM handle 1 allocated (16384 bytes),
              "3D resource 2 created with host backing",
              RESOURCE_INFO round-trip ok, EXECBUFFER accepted
  GPU_3D=0 -> "virtio-gpu 2D only" -> SKIP (77) -> gate FAIL

GET_CAPS still fails here, and it is the host, not this kernel: the
request provably matches what the host advertises (idx=0 -> id=1 ver=1
size=308), yet the host returns ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER from inside
virgl_renderer_get_capset.  This box's EGL resolves to NVIDIA's private
implementation, which initialises but cannot provide the offscreen
desktop-GL context virglrenderer needs; forcing Mesa's EGL moves the
failure earlier, to QEMU's own eglInitialize.  Recorded in the roadmap
because it reads exactly like a kernel bug and is not one.  The test
therefore reports GET_CAPS as a NOTE and does not assert on it.

What this does NOT prove: that anything was rendered.  The kernel does not
parse command streams, so "EXECBUFFER accepted" is a round trip, not a
render.  Pixel readback needs a stream matching virgl's command encoding,
which must be transcribed field by field rather than from memory.

98cb2fc79a2635726619e90d41fc416423fcc19a:
feat(gpu3d): unify command-stream limits and keep the gate reliable on busy hosts

Two problems, both found by running the gate rather than reading it.

The DRM VIRTGPU layer accepted command streams up to 16 MiB while the
driver refused anything over 128 KiB.  A 200 KiB stream -- well within
what Mesa actually produces -- would be accepted by the ioctl and then
fail deep inside the driver with -EINVAL, which is exactly the kind of
mismatch that costs an afternoon.  Replace both literals, and the stale
one in the legacy ioctl, with VIRTIO_GPU_3D_MAX_CMD_BYTES so the two
layers cannot drift apart again.  The submit path grows its staging
buffer on demand, so the limit is a sanity bound, not a structural one.

Second, the gate was timing-fragile: input_delay was 20s, and under host
load the TCG guest was still booting when the commands were typed, so
they landed before mksh existed and the run died with an empty log and a
SIGKILL.  It looked like a regression in this change and was not.  Raise
input_delay to 60s and the timeout to 240s; the guest is now reliably at
a shell before anything is injected.

Verified after both fixes: gate PASSes, and the log still shows GETPARAM
3D_FEATURES=1, capset mask=0x7, a GEM allocation, "3D resource 2 created
with host backing", a RESOURCE_INFO round trip, and an accepted
EXECBUFFER.
3dfdf43a137336c4ba201109c82c53c34cae2d6b:
docs(graphics): record the blocker is an old virglrenderer, not EGL vendor selection

The previous commit blamed this host's EGL vendor choice.  That was a
surface symptom and, being wrong, it would have sent whoever picked this
up to a dead end -- chasing EGL configuration on a machine where EGL was
never the problem.

Tested the full display-backend x EGL-vendor matrix instead of assuming:

  egl-headless  + NVIDIA EGL   -> boots, GETPARAM correct, GET_CAPS 0x1205
  gtk           + NVIDIA EGL   -> QEMU refuses: display backend has no GL
  gtk,gl=on     + NVIDIA EGL   -> boots, GL device attached, GET_CAPS 0x1205
  gtk,gl=on     + Mesa EGL     -> boots, GET_CAPS 0x1205

The third row is decisive: with gl=on the display backend *does* have
OpenGL, QEMU *does* attach the GL device, and it still fails.  So neither
the EGL vendor nor a missing display is the cause.  ("gl=on" is also
required for -device virtio-gpu-gl-* on a real display at all; without
it QEMU refuses outright, which is a useful fact on its own.)

The actual cause is the renderer:

  libvirglrenderer1:amd64 1.1.0-2
  capset[0] id=1 ver=1 size=308

308 bytes is the giveaway.  A modern virgl capset is kilobytes -- it has
to describe shader capabilities, format tables and parameter limits --
so this is a 2020-era renderer.  1.1.0 predates the protocol work Mesa
25.2 expects and cannot build the offscreen desktop GL context
virgl_renderer_get_capset needs, hence ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

Worth stating plainly: apt has no newer build to offer (Debian trixie's
only candidate is 1.1.0-2), so on this host the fix is either building
virglrenderer from source or changing host/distro.  That needs root and
is an environment change, so it is documented rather than done.

Also recorded: do not run `head -c1` against a /dev/dri node to test
access -- it blocks.  Use `test -r/-w`.

ed8bf17b9ca8a16ed6d350350d85823e5b5fc53a:
fix(kwx): downgrade every present 1 GiB slot, not just the first four

Rebuilding the x86_64 kernel from current source cannot boot at all: the
kernel panics with "init: no init program found", because the rootfs
lives on the second virtio-blk disk and virtio-blk is a drvmod that never
loads.

  [ERR] [DRVMOD] virtio-blk.a20drv: cannot mark module text executable
  [DRIVERMGR] /boot/drivers/virtio-blk.a20drv: module load failed (-12)
  [INIT] no ext4 device for /extra (ok without sdcard)

Every drvmod fails, not just one.  arch_kernel_wx_finalize() rebuilt only
PDPT slots 0..3, so a host with usable RAM above 4 GiB -- QEMU's default
8 GiB does -- leaves the higher slots as 1 GiB pages.  The buddy
allocator then hands a drvmod an order-7 (2 MiB) block from one of those
slots, x86_kwx_split_pmd() refuses to split a slot that still has PTE_PS,
and arch_kwx_module_protect() returns -ENOMEM.  Instrumented
confirmation:

  [KWX] split_pmd: no PD for va=0xffff80017fd75000 vpn2=5 pdpt=0x1400000e3
                    (vpn2=5 => 5-6 GiB, still a 1 GiB page)

The loop already skips absent and already-granular entries, so widening
the bound to the full 512-entry PDPT is the whole fix.

Note this is not caused by the GPU work on this branch: x86_64/mm/kwx.c
and drvmod/loader.c are byte-identical to main.  It arrived with the KXAN
commit 2d392f87 (2026-09-26); the working x86_64 kernel in the tree was
built 2026-09-21, five days earlier, which is why the regression was not
visible until the kernel was rebuilt.

After the fix: virtio-blk.a20drv loads, the distro rootfs is detected on
/extra, and the chroot proceeds.
90df56bf5ecd7d29cbfdf15877760dda25d1eed8:
fix(net): honor netif input ownership when freeing pbufs

The RX path called pbuf_free() when netif->input() returned an error, but
lwIP's ethernet_input() never reports an error that way: its error paths
do "goto free_and_return", which frees the pbuf itself and then returns
ERR_OK.  The vendored source states the contract outright --

  /* ... so the caller doesn't have to free it again */
  return ERR_OK;
  free_and_return:
    pbuf_free(p);
    return ERR_OK;

so the caller must not free.  The branch was unreachable today precisely
because ethernet_input always returns ERR_OK, which is why it had gone
unnoticed, but it is a latent double-free the moment any input path
returns a real error.

Not the cause of the observed "pbuf_free: p->ref > 0" panic -- that one
fires inside ip6_input and is tracked separately.
84ea1c25c6a1495474bb6b2436b0097ab631571f:
fix(net): guard the IPv6 recv-callback path so the socket layer builds without IPv6

lwip_raw_recv_cb() and lwip_udp_recv_cb() reached for ip6_current_dest_addr(),
ip6_current_header(), IP6H_HOPLIM() and IP6H_TC() unconditionally, so turning
LWIP_IPV6 off did not compile.  The pktinfo/hoplimit/tclass fields they fill are
IPv6-only by definition, so wrap both blocks in #if LWIP_IPV6 and leave the IPv4
path untouched.  With this the stack builds either way, which is what makes it
possible to bisect the IPv6 input path on its own.

cbebc6f2854e9c791bb787ed56cce409daa4c59b:
docs(graphics): record the CRTC ENOENT root cause -- fb_id aliases the GEM handle

Instrumenting alloc/free/addfb/setcrtc in one boot (with IPv6 off, otherwise the
known lwIP panic kills the session before a usable trace appears) shows the frame
buffer's backing GEM is freed while the frame buffer is still live:

    alloc h1 / free h1 / setcrtc fb_id=1 MISS live=0

drm_mode_addfb/addfb2 set fb.fb_id = b->handle, so the frame buffer id is just an
alias for the GEM handle; there is no frame buffer object and no refcount. Once
wlroots destroys the dumb buffer after AddFB2, as Linux semantics allow, the GEM
goes away and the fb_id dangles, so the following drmModeSetCrtc misses in
drm_find_gem() and returns -ENOENT. That also explains the intermittency: it
depends on whether destroy happens before setcrtc.

Note the fix is to give frame buffers their own ids and hold a reference, not to
special-case destroy_dumb, which would only postpone the dangling id.
2e2146a5f846abe38e847ffb9fa083c6e4c697c0:
fix(drm): assign framebuffer IDs and hold a reference to each GEM object

drm_mode_addfb/addfb2 set fb.fb_id = b->handle, so the framebuffer id was just an
alias of the GEM handle and no framebuffer object existed. Linux lets userspace
destroy the dumb buffer right after ADDFB2, which frees the GEM here, leaving the
framebuffer pointing at nothing; the next drmModeSetCrtc then fails in
drm_find_gem() with -ENOENT and the display never comes up. This is why the CRTC
failure was intermittent: it depends on whether destroy lands before setcrtc.

Introduce a drm_fb_t table with its own id counter. ADDFB/ADDFB2 allocate an fb_id
and take a reference on the GEM; SETCRTC and GETFB resolve through the fb table;
RMFB drops the reference, and the VMO is reclaimed only once the dumb handle is
gone and the last framebuffer reference is dropped. getresources enumerates the
fb table instead of the GEM table so its fb list matches the new id space.

Special-casing destroy_dumb would have been the tempting smaller patch, but it
would only postpone the dangling id rather than remove it.

Verified on the XFCE x86_64 image with NR_CPUS=4: 'Failed to set CRTC' goes from
17-20 occurrences to 0, the compositor reaches a real mode set, and xfdesktop
and xfsettingsd come up.

4cf851691ca59fead1732c82cbea09d9bd450cd7:
docs(net): narrow the lwIP pbuf double free, then record two refuted leads

The `pbuf_free: p->ref > 0` assertion on the x86_64 desktop image had two
candidate causes, and the assertion alone cannot tell them apart: it only proves
`ref == 0`, which is equally consistent with the same address being released
twice and with an adjacent pool element's `ref` being overwritten by an
out-of-bounds write. This thread settles that question, then works through the
hypotheses it opens, and ends with the free site still unidentified.

Instrumenting `pbuf.c` to remember freed addresses, forget them on reuse, and
compare at the assert site separates the two cases. The x86_64 `NR_CPUS=4` XFCE
run reports:

    pbufdiag: DOUBLE-FREE 0xffff80000147cba8 type=0 len=0 tot=2 next=0x0

The address really was freed before, so the adjacent-buffer-overrun theory is
ruled out. The freed pbuf's shape is the new lead: `len=0` with `tot_len=2` is
degenerate, and `len` reaching zero is what `pbuf_remove_header()` leaves behind
once it has consumed the whole payload. The IPv6 path calls it repeatedly, for
the IPv6 header and for the fragment header, which suggested a pbuf freed twice
after its header was stripped.

That first lead does not survive reading the vendored implementation.
`pbuf_remove_header()` frees nothing: it only moves the payload forward and
decrements `len`/`tot_len` in place. It also touches only the chain head rather
than walking `p->next`. Reading the code refutes the "freed out from under the
caller" theory, and it also explains the observed shape on its own terms: a head
pbuf of `len=0` and `next=0x0` whose remaining bytes sit in `tot_len`.

The hunt then moves to the two parties of a double free. `ip6_input`'s many
`pbuf_free()` calls all jump to `ip6_input_cleanup`, which always returns
`ERR_OK`, so that path is safe. The remaining risk is a branch that frees `p`
and returns an error, since `ethernet_input()` frees `p` again when the return is
not `ERR_OK`, which makes the `ERR_MEM` exits in `ip6_input` the sites to audit.
That second lead is refuted too: `ip6_input` has exactly five return points,
`ip6.c:535`, `541`, `561`, `581` and `1119`, and all five are `ERR_OK`. There is
no `ERR_MEM` exit, so the `ethernet_input` error path never runs for IPv6.

With both obvious candidates excluded, the established facts are that
`ip6_input` never returns an error, that a chain-head pbuf can legitimately be
reduced to `len=0`/`next=0x0` by `pbuf_remove_header()`, and that at assert time
`ref` is 0 for an address that really was freed. IPv6-only remains the strongest
lead, because the same `ethernet_input` path never trips for IPv4, which places
the difference inside `ip6_input` rather than at the entry point. The next step
recorded is to log every `pbuf_free` in `ip6_input` and dump the recent free
sequence at the panic.

That full probe, over all 22 `pbuf_free` sites in `ip6_input` on the x86_64
`NR_CPUS=4` XFCE image, then produced a false positive. It caught

    ip6diag: REPEAT-FREE 0xffff80000139aa00 already in recent frees
    ip6diag:   ==> 0xffff80000139aa00
    ip6diag:       0xffff80000139aa70

but the `pbuf_free: p->ref > 0` assertion did not fire in that same run, zero
times. The repeated free was legitimate: that pbuf had `ref > 0`, most likely
because `pbuf_ref` had given it two owners.

Two lessons stay on the record. Judging a double free by address alone misreads
normal refcounting as a defect, so any future check must log `p->ref` alongside
the address. And the two addresses differ by exactly `0x70`, the size of
`struct pbuf`, so they are adjacent pool elements. That is suggestive of the
neighbour-overrun shape, but address adjacency alone proves nothing, since the
pool is contiguous by construction.

The follow-up left undone is to widen each record to
`{address, ref, call site}` and dump the sequence only on a run where the
assertion actually fires. Reproduction requires SLAAC to stay enabled.
47fe5f89107e77d7f2fb31851f84ba14e5738636:
docs(kernel): correct four comments that actively mislead a debugger

All four were defects where the comment asserted something the code does
not do, which is worse than having no comment at all.

riscv64/trap_frame.h: the arch_ptrace_export_regs() comment described a
Linux user_regs_struct mapping (x[1..31] into regs[0..], pc inside regs[])
that the code never performs, and contradicted itself halfway through. The
generic register file is arch-ordered; the ABI reorder lives in
linux_arch_regs_export() in platform/arch_hooks.c. State that, plus why
x[0] is kept and why orig_syscall needs a slot of its own.

x86_64/trap_frame.h: padding[2] carried live state -- the per-task kernel
stack top and the user FS base -- under a name that said it was inert.
Rename to kernel_stack_top / user_fs_base. TRAP_CTX_TP and the
set/get_kernel_stack accessors are the only C-side users and all keep
working; trap.S addresses the slots by offset and only its annotations
change.

vDSO getcpu: all five kernel/vdso/<arch>/vdso.S stubs stored CPU 0 under a
signature-only comment that read like a working implementation, while the
getcpu syscall returns the true cpu_current_id(). A program resolving
getcpu through the vDSO sees CPU 0 on an SMP guest. Document it once in
kernel/include/mm/vdso.h -- the only header all five .S files can be
pointed at -- and leave a short pointer at each definition. That header
also claimed the vDSO is riscv64-only; five arches implement it.

virtio DMA ordering: virtio_blk cleans the ring before publishing,
virtio_net cleans after, virtio_gpu cleans the whole avail ring. All
three are correct, because arch_dma_sync_for_device() cleans a cache line
rather than ordering the store stream. The hazard is a future reader
harmonising them, so state the contract once in the shared virtq.h and
cross-reference both call sites. Also document the virtio-blk status-byte
arithmetic, where the +1 and the 0xFF submit sentinel are one wire-format
invariant and S_OK == 0 makes that sentinel load-bearing.
