1a21d3bf26a13cd218f5314bc8a065427332fd74:
feat(net): add interrupt-driven e1000, RTL8139, and MSI-X affinity

E1000's completion path becomes interrupt-driven by default: it requests
MSI-X (falling back to INTx) before it opens IMS, keeps pure polling when
no vector is available or when a20.e1000.poll=1 is on the command line,
and frees the handler on remove. The RX ISR drains the ring in one pass
rather than in per-packet budgeted chunks, and TX now mirrors TDH to
release descriptors -- the old code cleared DD and never reset it, so the
ring failed permanently after its first wrap.

Added rtl8139.c, which claims PCI 10ec:8139 and the ethernet controller
class. No driver matched that device before, so `-nic user,model=rtl8139`
came up with no NET device at all. TX uses four TSAD/TSD descriptors and
a 64 KiB RX ring in one page-aligned allocation; the handler is registered
before IMR is unmasked, so an interrupt arriving during probe is
acknowledged and dropped instead of touching a half-configured ring.

On x86_64, arming an MSI-X vector on a secondary CPU needs that CPU's own
LAPIC page, so the request goes out as an IPI (IRQ_VECTOR_MSIX_VECTOR);
irqchip.c programs the LVT through it and restores the caller's IRQ state.

Added pci_msix_set_affinity()/pci_msix_set_all_affinity() and the
/proc/a20/irq_affinity interface. The default target is still the boot
CPU and the entry layout is bit-for-bit what it was, so an unmatched
affinity behaves exactly as before.

tcp_accept_test gains a serve mode: hostfwd does not deliver to loopback,
so the NIC gates have to bind the guest's real address. The loopback
client is skipped in that mode -- it would connect to a listener that
never saw the wire and report a pass for a connection that crossed
nothing.

Gates: smoke-net-e1000-irq and smoke-net-rtl8139 both PASS on x86_64 QEMU
(hostfwd round trip 18091/18093, mode=irq, interrupt and reclaim
counters > 0), and smoke-msix-x86_64 PASSes under -smp 2 with delivery
migrated to CPU1. Neither NIC has run on real silicon; the RTL8139
register map and ring geometry come from QEMU's device model.
8bf9d03dd910bf221570c495bc2b8862bcd5c935:
feat(block): complete requests by interrupt for AHCI, virtio-scsi, and virtio-blk

All three now take the interrupt by default and keep polling available as a
fallback. AHCI opens PxIE and GHC.IE only once request_irq() has accepted the
line; virtio-scsi enables its queue's interrupt bit under the same condition.
a20.ahci.poll=1 and a20.virtio-scsi.poll=1 force the polling path instead, so
an image can be booted on a machine whose IRQ routing is not yet known to be
right. virtio-blk has no cmdline switch -- it walks a three-step ladder
(MSI-X per queue, then the shared INTx line, then polling) and each step is
entered only when the previous one failed.

The two paths have to be distinguishable from outside, or "the disk works"
says nothing about whether the interrupt path works at all: the poll hook
moves the same work, so a driver with a completely dead interrupt path still
looks healthy. /proc/a20/perf therefore counts AHCI's two paths separately
(ahci_irq_completions vs ahci_poll_completions), and the smoke-ahci-ich9 gate
requires poll == 0 -- every completion must have gone through the top-half.

virtio-scsi exposes the same split through A20_BLK_IOCTL_GET_STATS instead
(irq_count / irq_completions / spin_completions), because its counters live in
the block stats path rather than /proc/a20/perf. virtio-blk has no such split
yet; that gap is recorded in docs/drivers/meta/implementation-status.md.

Each driver also frees its handler on remove, and virtio_snd's setup_queue
takes the device so it stops dropping the instance while arming a queue.

Added virtio_scsi_test, which writes, flushes and reads back through the
real block path; the first record with a corrupt WRITE flag and the second
with flags cleared to 0 each make it fail, so a pass means the write really
reached the medium. It asserts irq_mode is MSI-X or INTx and that irq_count
grew, so a run that silently fell back to polling fails rather than passes.

Gates: smoke-ahci-ich9 PASS (one ich9-ahci port bound on the interrupt path,
12 commands, all 12 completed through the IRQ top-half) and
smoke-virtio-scsi-irq PASS on x86_64 QEMU. Real SATA PHY and IRQ delivery on
unsiliconed hardware remain unverified.
f3af3faed60ecfa6a660ac7f064b1ae3c714682c:
feat(char): add virtio console and random-number devices

virtio-console exposes virtio-serial port 0 as a CHAR device. It negotiates
VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1 only and deliberately does not negotiate MULTIPORT, so
the device side has exactly one port and needs no multiport control
protocol: q0 carries rx, q1 carries tx, and there is no control queue.
Receive is interrupt-driven over INTx, with an automatic read/poll drain if
request_irq() fails; transmit is synchronous with a single descriptor in
flight and a 2 s bounded wait that releases the instance lock while it
waits. Received bytes are mirrored into console input by default, which
VPORT_IOCTL_SET_CONSOLE turns off.

virtio-rng reads VIRTIO_ID_RNG into /dev/hwrng and folds what it reads
into the kernel pool (random_reseed), which sys_getrandom, ASLR and stack
canaries already draw on. Both PCI (1af4:1044 and the transitional 1005)
and virtio-mmio work. Buffers are attached on demand rather than kept
posted: QEMU's virtio_rng_process() requests exactly the byte count the
avail ring advertises, so permanently posting the buffers would mean
draining host entropy on every probe with nobody reading. An empty byte
ring makes read() notify and then spin for a bounded 500 ms, returning
-ETIMEDOUT instead of parking, so a device that never answers cannot wedge
a reader. Entropy reaches the pool only on the read path, never from the
ISR, because arch_entropy_sample() reads proc_current().

Both are single static instances; a second function returns -EBUSY. Neither
uses MSI-X, and neither has been run off QEMU -- riscv64, aarch64 and
loongarch64 have had syntax checks only.

Gates: smoke-virtio-console PASS (64 bytes host->guest->/dev/vport0->host)
and smoke-virtio-rng PASS (HWRNG_TEST bytes=256, entropy not all-zero or
single-byte) on x86_64 QEMU. hwrng_test fails on all-zero, all-ones or
single-byte-repeated output, so the pass means real entropy came back.
a5425bc069d9e3b3aaf5f37330cb8ffe06e14826:
feat(mmc): use the board IRQ for dw-sdio data transfers and poll without an IRQ

The data plane previously polled forever, so the cost of every transfer sat
on the boot CPU. It now claims the board's IRQ resource when one is
published: a bounded pre-poll, then park on a wait_queue until the handler
wakes it. Polling stays the behaviour whenever platform_device_irq() has
nothing to return (the riscv64 FDT enumerator builds RES_IRQ from the
device tree's `interrupts`), when a20.dw-sdio.poll=1 asks for it, or when
request_irq() refuses the line -- and a completion timeout downgrades the
instance to polling permanently, so a wrong interrupt number costs
throughput rather than a wedged SD card. A park is always bounded, so a
wake that never arrives becomes a re-check rather than a hang.

Card enumeration (dw_sdio_init_dev) stays polled even with an IRQ claimed:
probe runs from kernel_main or a kthread and must not park for the whole
bring-up.

The transfer lock is now a mutex rather than the old spinlock, because a
park cannot happen with interrupts disabled. The handler resolves the
instance from the device rather than from a file-static pointer, and the
visionfive2 board publishes the SDIO IRQ resource so the path is reachable
on that board.

Two gates cover this: smoke-platform-irq-fallback PASS (poll_only fallback
stays coherent) and smoke-driver-lifecycle PASS. QEMU has no dw-mshc
device model, so the interrupt path itself is unverified on real hardware;
the VF2 interrupt line number comes from the DTB shipped with the image.

78fcb778191d6c97413e5349950734c430a88de0:
feat(time): add an MC146818 CMOS RTC as the x86_64 wall clock

The wall clock previously started from a compile-time constant
(A20_BUILD_UNIX_TIME), so a guest's date was the date the kernel was built,
not the date the machine booted. cmos-rtc.a20drv reads the MC146818 and hands
the result to timekeeping_wallclock_set_hw(), replacing that seed. Both x86_64
boards declare the platform device at IOPORT 0x70/0x71.

It handles both BCD and binary counter formats and waits for UIP to clear
before reading, so a read does not catch the chip mid-update. The century byte
at CMOS 0x32 is not trustworthy across firmware -- some leave it 0x00 -- so a
value outside 19xx/20xx is taken as 20xx and logged.

Read-only by design: it writes no CMOS register, so there is no RTC_SET_TIME
path back into hardware, and it takes no interrupt, sampling once when it binds
rather than tracking the seconds tick. There is no RTC class in the unified
model (driver_class.h has char/block/net/input/display/audio), so it binds as
DEV_CLASS_NONE and readers get the time through timekeeping_get_realtime(),
/dev/rtc and /proc/stat's btime. No timezone conversion is done -- whatever
CMOS holds is what the guest reports.

Gate: smoke-rtc-cmos PASS. It boots with -rtc base=utc so the host and guest
clocks are comparable, and a host-side post-step (tools/check_rtc_wallclock.py
--max-skew 300) re-reads the guest's /bin/date output and compares it against
the host. Log .kernel-build/smoke/rtc-cmos-x86_64.log: the guest adopted
epoch 1791231484 against the build-time seed 1791230264, so the hardware read
is what is actually in use. The gate asserts both the seed line and the
adoption line, because the driver is an Early DriverStore module and can only
bind after driver_manager_early_init() -- seeing only one of the two would not
show that the replacement happened.

smoke-rtc-cmos-fallback (CMOS set outside the acceptable window, driver must
bind anyway and keep the build-time seed) has NOT been run. Only the first
gate has runtime evidence.

830d6606008ce17224545c2f7b43d1888c9bd1e6:
feat(kernel): add kernel preemption behind CONFIG_KERNEL_PREEMPT

Cooperative kernel code can now lose the CPU at a hardware-interrupt
return: after arch_handle_irq() completes, kernel_preempt_at_irq_return()
switches out the interrupted task when need_resched is pending, the task
is RUNNING and not idle, and the interrupted context ran with interrupts
enabled (per-arch ARCH_IRQ_WAS_ENABLED_IN_TRAP against the saved status
register).  The resume path needs no new assembly: the preempted task's
kstack still holds its trap frame under the handler frames, so __switch
back into it unwinds through the ordinary IRQ epilogue.

Two invariants make the per-CPU preempt counter sound without per-task
save/restore: sched() masks interrupts across pick->publish->__switch
(each task restores its own flag state at out:, because __switch already
saves/restores flags per task), and context_switch_locked() panics if
ever entered with the counter raised -- a voluntary switch under a
spinlock was already banned by the lock contract, this makes it a checked
fact.  spin_lock/spin_unlock/spin_trylock_irqsave now bracket every
critical section with preempt_disable/enable; waiting for a lock stays
preemptible.

Hosted arches get the hook by default; the MCU profile (armv7m PendSV)
keeps its cooperative scheduler, and a hosted build missing the hook is
a compile error rather than a silent never-preempts.

Also: ppc64le trap dispatch learned to route kernel-mode traps to
kernel_trap_handler() by SRR1[PR] (previously every trap took the user
path, so kernel ticks were charged as user time and the preemption point
was unreachable), and BUILD_VARIANT gains -preempt so pre-merge build
directories cannot be reused with stale no-preemption objects.

cow.c guards its per-PTE status sidecar calls with ARCH_HAS_PGTABLE_OPS
(arm32's short-descriptor backend has none) so the arm32 build gets past
mm/fork again.

Verification: check-*-bringup for x86_64, riscv64, aarch64, riscv32,
loongarch64, ppc64le; smoke-* for the same six; smoke-smp-bringup;
smoke-abi-linux; RT-wakeup A/B probe (user/cmds/core/preempt_lat.c)
under TCG on x86_64 and riscv64, smp=1 and smp=2 pinned and unpinned:
max wakeup 557ms -> 21ms (x86_64 smp1), 1ms (x86_64 smp2), 427ms -> 31ms
(riscv64 smp1), 10ms (riscv64 smp2) against preempt-off controls.
5d8c60992b382e77824ab2c43e65fed802c2bccf:
fix(mm.fs): fix the defects found while getting minecraft to start

A20OS could boot a Minecraft JVM but the client never reached the main
menu.  Chasing that down turned up a set of independent defects; this
commit carries the ones that are real on their own terms.

mm/madvise: a huge leaf that straddles either end of the request was
dropped wholesale.  pt_unmap_leaf() discards the whole leaf, so pages
outside [addr, end) -- and outside the VMA -- went with it, and the
cursor then stepped past them.  munmap.c, mprotect.c and mremap.c all
demote the leaf first; madvise was the one that did not.

fdtable: MAX_FILES was 1024, and RLIMIT_NOFILE is hard-clamped to it,
so no process could hold more than 1024 descriptors.  A Minecraft JVM
keeps roughly three thousand asset files open across the resource
reload and simply ran out.  Raise the ceiling to 4096 and move the two
MAX_FILES-sized scratch arrays in fdtable_files_put() and
fdtable_close_on_exec() onto the heap: at 4096 they are 32 KiB each,
against a 64 KiB kernel stack.  Both now also handle allocation
failure by closing in place rather than leaking the vfile pointers.

Also carried over from the same investigation, each a genuine bug:
mm/fault.c truncated file_pos to int; fs/block_cache.c returned the
wrong page on a miss; fs/page_cache.c memset a pinned page; mm/vm.c
left dead-code PTE changes un-converged with the TLB.

0f367e827dc46d1561dcb1a82d1ad30b2d196f25:
feat(mm): bring huge leaves into the single-level model

pt_map_huge() wrote the 2 MiB leaf PTE but never its status slot, fork's
parent-side COW sync stopped at level 0, and cow_sync_status() peeked a
level-0 slot for a leaf that lives one level up -- a huge page was
invisible to the model that claims every mapping.

Measured on smoke-mm-stress: the THP fault path had NEVER fired.  The
decline was -EEXIST from a level-0 table left behind by earlier 4K
faulting in the same 2 MiB block, empty in every observed case
(live-children=0), and invisible to the caller because pt_lookup_leaf()
answers for the (absent) 4K entry, not the table.  An empty child is now
retired under parent-then-child node locks and the huge leaf installed;
a child holding any live or swapped entry still refuses.

Non-vacuity: huge_install counts every install as a plain global printed
in [MM-ASM] (a20_perf stays dormant until a /proc read arms it, and the
process owning the huge leaf has exited before the shutdown audit), and
the auditor counts present level>0 leaves as huge=.  smoke-mm-stress now
asserts audit-all-zero AND huge_install>=1; its huge phases map twice the
size and fault a 2 MiB-aligned window so the THP conditions can actually
hold.  Before this commit every huge gate passed on 4K pages.
3b600730c53c3d73f3b4491d634adae1a0fcf55b:
feat(mm): break shared anonymous COW pages without mm- lock

MM_COW_FROM_STATUS -- the second lockless slice of the fault path, after
the pre-provisioned anon install.  A write fault on a leaf whose status
says ANON_MAPPED with the COW bit copies the frame and swaps the PTE
under the leaf lock alone; mm_cursor_replace_if_cow() re-verifies the
PTE (still COW, still this frame) inside that lock and re-derives the
new flags from the old PTE, so a concurrent mprotect between the
unlocked observation and the install is honoured, not overwritten.

The rc==1 in-place upgrade stays on the mm->lock path on purpose: making
the last reference writable must exclude fork's frame_get, which
serialises under mm->lock, and an unneeded copy is waste, never a bug.

That lock only excludes what takes it, so the competing writers were
brought under the same node lock with an under-lock re-check:
- fork's parent-side COW rewrite (both clone sites), which previously
  rewrote *src from a value read before any lock the fast path honours;
- mprotect's present-leaf rewrite and its never-faulted status refresh,
  the latter guarding the status byte the lockless paths read.

Two defects the first version had, both found at runtime:
- frame_get() inside the pfa.lock critical section self-deadlocked
  (LOCK-STALL, waiter in handle_cow_fault, holder pfa.lock); the pin is
  now a manual refcount increment under the same lock frame_get would
  take.
- pfa_alloc_page() is the reclaiming allocator; its victim teardown
  wants the node locks the path holds.  pfa_alloc_flags(0,0), the same
  rule the anon fast path documents.

Non-vacuity: mm_cow_from_status_count is a plain global printed in
[MM-ASM] and smoke-mm-stress asserts cow_from_status>=1 (41 in the
passing run) alongside huge_install>=1.  check-mm-pt-lock-order grows
five assertions pinning the lock triangle (fork bracket+recheck x2,
mprotect bracket x2, non-reclaiming allocation, before-mm->lock order).
fork and mprotect join the MM_AS_CURSOR_ONLY_ENTRY bypass list with
what actually holds them safe.
